### CHAPTER V: GOOD GOVERNANCE

Financial institutions are particularly vulnerable to conflict of interest allegations given the
inherent nature of their business and their reliance on the continued confidence and goodwill
of depositors and borrowers alike.

 The Staff involved in Credit Underwriting and Approval should behave ethically in all credit
activities, declare and refrain from participating in a credit decisions involving potential
conflict of interests.  Conflict of interest, accusations against directors, officers and employees
of this Bank are to be avoided if public confidence in the Bank is to be maintained.

 Conflict of interest exists whenever directors, officers or employees benefit directly or
indirectly from the approval or operation of services given to a customer of the Bank.  Direct
benefit exists when the party in question accepts gifts in consideration of providing services
and facilities or has a direct beneficial ownership in the client company.  Indirect benefit exists
when the benefit of these transactions passes to the directors, officers or employees’ families
or business partners.  Hence, to maintain good governance in the Bank, directors, officers and
employees will not only avoid these situations but will, in so far as possible, take actions which
will avoid even the appearance of conflict of interest.  Further, NRB provisions regarding Good
Governance to be followed by all concerned during credit approval process.

### CHAPTER XVI: LOAN PROVISIONS, COLLECTION,
 RECOVERY AND WRITE OFF

##### Loan Loss Provisioning

a. The term ‘Loan Loss Provisioning’ refers to the non-cash expenses made by the Bank

to account for future losses on loan defaults.  Provisioning of loans will be done as per
the loan classification prescribed by Nepal Rastra Bank.
 b. The Bank may, at the discretion of management, set higher provisioning than that of

regulatory requirements as a prudent practice based on the risk profile of the individual
borrower, group of borrower or specific products/portfolio.

 Similarly, the Bank may reschedule and restructure the loan at the written request of the
customer along with business plan being submitted by the client, subject to the Bank being
convinced with the reason for doing so with reasonable assurance on the loan being repaid.
 Reschedule and restructure of the loan shall be done being within the broader framework as
laid down by NRB directives and provisioning to such rescheduled/ restructured accounts shall
be done as per the guidelines laid by NRB directives.

 ##### Loan Collection and Recovery

Concerned branch officials are responsible for continuous follow up for the settlement of any
due (including interest or principal) as per the terms and conditions.

 Concerned branch officials shall make rigorous follow up for settlement of overdue.  Recovery
action of classified accounts or other accounts shall be guided by the Loan Recovery Procedure
of the Bank and subsequent amendments therein.  Further, loan call back, auction notice
publishing, income recognition of default accounts etc.  shall also be as per Loan Recovery
Procedures of the Bank.

 ##### Loan Write Off 

The process and decision for writing-off of loans/advances and interest shall be guided by the
Loan Write off By-laws and Loan Recovery Procedures of the Bank.

### CHAPTER XVII: MISCELLANEOUS

##### 17.1 Approval and Effective Date

This Policy shall come into immediate effect upon approval by the Board of Directors.

 ##### 17.2 Repeal and Saving

metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.creator: Microsoft® Word 2016
metadata.window:
**1. ** **Introduction**

Global IME Bank Ltd.  (GIBL) demands the highest standards of integrity and ethical conduct in its
business dealing.  The Bank will not tolerate any bribery or corrupt practices related to its business
activities from its employees or business partners.  It is committed to transparent reporting and
adopting all other reasonable measures which avoid employee's involvement in bribery or corruption.

 **2. ** **Scope**

GIBL has a vision and core values that are incompatible with bribery and corruption.  This AntiBribery & Corruption Policy applies to all Bank's activities in all jurisdictions in which it operates.
 This policy applies to all the board members and all staffs (which includes temporary as well as
contract staff) of the Bank wherever they are located.  This policy commits to conduct banking service
ethically and with the utmost integrity in all its operations throughout the world.

 The management of the Bank shall ensure that its bribery prevention policies and procedures are
understood by all staff of the Bank through internal and external communication, including training,
in proportion to the risks.

 **3. ** **Purpose**

The purpose of this Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy is to provide Bank's staff including director,
agents, consultants and contractors as well as suppliers involved in the Bank's activities must be aware
and become familiar with a clear set of guidelines to ensure that the Bank conducts its activities in an
ethical and appropriate manner as well as complying with the laws and regulations of each jurisdiction
in which it operates.  The policy aims to:

a) Outline principles for conducting business with integrity and in accordance with the highest

ethical standards;

b) Provide guidance on the types of behavior that may give rise to violation of anti-bribery and anti
corruption laws;

c) Ensure that the financial and other resources of the Bank are used solely for proper purposes;

d) Promote a culture of honesty and openness among the Bank's staff.

 Bribery and corruption undermine the rule of law and the principle of fair competition.  The Bank’s
staff can take practical steps to mitigate the inherent risk of corrupt behaviors.  This policy aims to
inform the Bank’s staffs about Bank’s intention to closely monitor corruption risk and to take
immediate action if evidence of corrupt activity is suspected.

 **4. ** **Definition**

**Corruption: Corruption is the abuse of position and/or trust to get an improper advantage or gain. **

**Bribe:** Money or favor given or promised in order to influence the judgment or conduct of a
person in a position of trust.  It may involve a monetary payment or offer; it covers anything of value
such as:

a) Cash or cash equivalents (e.g., gift vouchers or loans);

b) Some gifts, hospitality, entertainment or travel;

g) Anything else that is of value to the recipient.

 **[Bribery: Bribery is the act of influencing the judgment of others by offering money or](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/offering)**
[something valuable in order to persuade them to do something for undue benefits.  It involves (either](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/valuable)
directly or indirectly) improperly offering or providing a benefit or something of value to a public
official, someone in business or a close relative of such a person in order to obtain or retain business
or an advantage or to induce or reward improper conduct or an improper decision.

 **Prohibited Payments: It includes any offer, gift or payment or authorization of an offer, any money**
or thing of value for the undue benefit to the bank /any government/corporate official/director or
employees or any other person.

 **Gift: A gift or a present is an item given/ received.  It includes any item (cash/kinds), or any service. **
Solicitation or acceptance of gifts, gratuities, special favors, and/ or entertainment from prospective,
current, or former Bank customers, suppliers, and other persons or entities doing business with or
seeking to do business with the Bank or which could be viewed in any way as seeking to influence the
Bank’s business is prohibited.

 c) The Bank will assess the nature and extent of its exposure to potential external and internal risks

of bribery on its behalf by persons associated with it.  This risk assessment would be done
annually by the Human Resource Department (HRD) and report to General Compliance and Good
Governance Unit and appropriate measures shall be taken.

 d) HRD shall assign ABC officer to monitor staffs account and any incidents occurred.

 e) On assessing the nature of the service performed by a supplier, contractor or agent, the Bank shall

perform services for or on behalf of the Bank, in order to mitigate such bribery risks.

 **7. ** **Roles and Responsibilities**

**a)** **Board of Directors**

The responsibilities of the Board with regard to anti-bribery and corruption shall include:

i. Ensuring that the Bank’s management implements this policy and process in order to maintain

zero-tolerance tone and high integrity in the Bank.

 ii.  Establishing the good governance system and providing guidance to Bank's management.

 iii.  Ensuring that an effective framework for managing bribery and corruption is in place.

 **b)** **Management**

Management shall be accountable and responsible for the implementation of this policy, its
implementation with compliance in the Bank with following major roles and responsibilities:

i. Encouraging a transparent and ethical culture within the Bank.

 ii.  Regularly monitoring and appropriate risk assessment of its business activities.

 **2. ** **Action against Bribery & Corruption**

GIBL staff should have sound understanding of this policy and undertake the task
accordingly.  Violation of this code would render them liable for disciplinary proceedings.
 Every employee and related stakeholders mentioned in this policy shall be bounded by
different Acts and regulations.  Along with this policy, the following Acts and Laws shall be
applicable for actions against identified bribery and corruption:

a) The Prevention of Corruption Act, 2059

b) Banking Offense and Punishment Act, 2064

c) GIBL Code of Conduct

d) Assets (Money) Laundering Prevention Act 2064

e) Other applicable laws, acts and regulations of the land.

 **9. ** **Compliance Procedure**

The Anti-bribery and corruption policy implies to every individual associated with the Bank’s
operation.  It should be strictly complied for the mitigation of various threats of bribery and corruption
within the Bank.  The following compliance procedure shall be supportive to identify and mitigate
bribery and corruption related risks:

**a)** **Risk Assessment**

The Bank faces the threat of reputation risk due to incidents of bribery and corruption in the
regular course of business, through the use of business partners, gifts and hospitality, and its
own employees.  An initial assessment of the risk across the various functions of the Bank
shall be done and adequate bribery prevention procedures in proportion to the risks that the
Bank faces would be drawn.  Satisfactory Anti-bribery and corruption laws and a good
enforcement system would support sound performance.

 Effective risk assessment lies at the core of the success or failure of this policy as this points
out the specific areas in which the Bank faces bribery and corruption risks and allows the
management to evaluate and mitigate these risks.  The major risks are detailed below:

**i. ** **Transaction Risk**

Risk of loss due to any transactions resulting into the adverse financial impact on the
Bank.  The transaction risk may arise in the both operation as well as business
function of the Bank.

**ii. ** **Outsourcing Risk**

It is the risk posed by the service providers, agents and their employees with regard to
anti-bribery and corruption to secure the contract or orders or information or data to
other third parties.  The outsourcing risk may arise in the Bank while dealing with
outsourcing companies and agents.

 **iii. ** **Employee Risk**

For any service provider institution, the employees form the corner stone and if they
are corrupt or if their integrity is doubtful, it could lead a bad culture within the Bank
and would leave an indelible mark on the Bank.  The Bank faces a big risk in the form
of employee risk.

 The employee risk is higher in functions such as loans in projects and to corporate
houses is provided in huge amount and also during procurement of goods involving
considerable amount.  All kinds of unethical HR activities, such as offering
employment or internship, promotions and trainings are often deemed to be
something of value and therefore giving, offering, promising such in order to obtain
or retain an undue business advantage is considered bribery and corruption.

 **iv. ** **Gifts and Hospitality**

Gifts and hospitality in professional life are a high-risk area for bribery.  At times gifts
become inducements, which can be a form of bribery.  This Policy does not prohibit
normal and appropriate gifts and hospitality (given or received, in accordance with
GIBL Code of Conduct).  However, the gifts and hospitality with persons having
personal relationship shall be acceptable where there is no business/ professional
benefit (with wrong intension) and shall be distinguished from professional life/
relationship.

 **b)** **Risk Mitigation**

To mitigate the various risks posed and in order to maintain its high ethical standards and
protect its reputation against any allegation of bribery and corruption and to ensure that the
transactions and activities of the Bank personnel to comply with the law, the Bank shall take
up the following risk mitigation measures:

The staff should operate business in compliance with the highest professional integrity and
ethical standards and with the laws of all countries.

 i. Use of Bank’s funds for unlawful, improper or unethical purpose is prohibited.

 ii.  The Bank may not authorize, promise, encourage or make any prohibited payments,
regardless of amount, in the course of the Bank’s business.  This prohibition also
applies to indirect contributions, payments/gifts through consultants, contractors, subcontractors, agents, sub-agents, sponsors or sub-sponsors, joint venture partners,
advisors, customers, suppliers or other third parties.

 iii.  The Bank’s staff may not either directly or indirectly, give, or agree to give, offer or
receive any money, gift or thing of value to or from any government/corporate
official/director or employee or its representative, or to or from any director or
manager of any corporate or any other person or party as an inducement or reward for
favorable action or forbearance from action or the exercise of influence.  For the

metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.creator: Microsoft® Word 2016
metadata.window:
purposes of this Policy, a "representative" includes any person employed by or acting
for another, and "party" includes an employer.

 iv.  No payment to any party or its representative may be made in cash or other than by
wire transfer or cheque to a bank account in such party's or its representative's name
except as per the provision mentioned in the Financial Administration Rule (FAR) of
the Bank.

 v. As money laundering legislation covers proceeds of crimes, ABC officer will monitor
the transactions in the accounts and where there is actual knowledge or suspicion that
the funds in the account may be associated with taking of bribe and/or corruption it
shall be necessary to report such activity to the Human Resource Department (HRD).

 vi.  The Bank’s internal audit department shall make a report on any bribery or corruption
suspected or detected by it during the course of its audit.  Such reports shall be
notified to General Compliance and Good Governance Unit through HRD and further
action shall be taken based on the report, including termination of the contract with
contractor.

 vii.  The code of conduct issued by HR department shall be strictly followed by all
employees.

 Any employee found guilty of indulge in bribery and corrupt practices would be subjected to
the Bank’s internal disciplinary proceedings and action taken accordingly.

 **c)** **Due Diligence**

Due diligence is an element of corporate good governance and it is envisaged that due
diligence related to bribery prevention will often form part of a wider due diligence
framework of the Bank.  Due diligence procedures serve as a tool for mitigating the
outsourcing, business associate or agent risk.  Due diligence of specific prospective third-party
intermediaries could significantly mitigate these risks.  The due diligence of staff suspected in
bribery and corruption activities shall be conducted by ABC officer and report to HRD.  The
procedure would be in proportion to the Bank’s assessment of the risk with the following:

i. Considerable care should be exercised while entering into new business relationships;

ii.  Continued monitoring and appraisal of the existing relationships.

 iii.  Due care to be exercised over change of personnel deployed for the outsourced work
by the service provider.

 iv.  Due diligence of employees would be taken before employing them and contract of
employment offered only if the due diligence is found satisfactory.

 **d)** **Monitoring, Reporting and Supervision**

The bribery risks that the Bank faces may change over time with the nature and scale of its
activities.  The procedures required to mitigate those risks are also likely to change.  The
internal audit department would also cover the monitoring of incidence of bribery or
corruption during the course of the regular audits.  The Bank may step up its vigil on its noninterest expenditure to monitor unusual increases if any in expenses to detect bribery.  The
Bank will also monitor the ethical quality of transactions, such as internal financial control
mechanisms, will help provide insight into the effectiveness of procedures designed to
prevent bribery.  Such function would be under taken by the internal audit department of the
Bank.

metadata.title: Anti-Bribery and Corruption Policy (ABC Policy)
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.creator: Microsoft® Word 2016
metadata.window:
HRD shall be responsible for reporting the incidents of bribery / corruption to General
Compliance and Good Governance Unit.  The unit shall further investigate and verify the
reported incidents and shall submit report with recommendation to CEO for appropriate
actions.  An annual report on the incidents of bribery and corruption and areas of concern if
any shall be submitted by General Compliance and Good Governance Unit for addressing the
risk at the apex level.

 **e)** **Training and Awareness**

i. All new employees shall be imparted a general awareness training of "The Prevention
of Corruption Act 2059" & "Banking offense and Punishment Act, 2064" relating
with this policy and their responsibilities under the act as a part of their induction
training.  HRD shall arrange the awareness training on bribery and corruption on
regular basis and focus to be provided to those staff working on major controlling
areas (procurement process, credit areas etc.)  for bribery and corruption.

 ii.  Intermittently employees would be made aware of the responsibilities in case of
changes in the regulations or the act and the expectations of the Bank’s management
from them vide internal communications.

 iii.  The staff shall follow the Bank's "Whistle Blowing Policy" to raise their voice in case
of bribery and corruption.  The Bank is committed to maintain a culture of the highest
ethics and to comply with the Bank's Code of Conduct (COC).  The Bank encourages
all staff and stakeholders to raise a genuine concern.

 iv.  Persons associated with business and outsourcing agents as well as vendors and
suppliers will also be provided with awareness of the Bank’s Anti-bribery policy.

 v. The trainings regarding anti-bribery and corruption shall be provided on regular basis
to entire employees (including drivers, messenger, cleaner, tea maid, security guards)
of the Bank.  It shall also be communicated regularly to related stakeholders of the
Bank.

 **10. ** **Record Keeping**

All records pertaining to concerns shall be retained for a period of at least five (5) years.

 **11. ** **Review of the Policy**

The Bank shall monitor and review the anti-bribery policy upon approval from the Board as and when
required to prevent bribery and corruption in the Bank by persons associated with it and make
improvements as necessary from time to time.  The Bank shall monitor the effectiveness and review
the implementation of this policy, considering its suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.  Any
deficiencies identified shall be rectified.

-----

to entire employees (including drivers, messenger, cleaner, tea maid, security guards)
of the Bank.  It shall also be communicated regularly to related stakeholders of the
Bank.

 **10. ** **Record Keeping**

All records pertaining to concerns shall be retained for a period of at least five (5) years.

 **11. ** **Review of the Policy**

The Bank shall monitor and review the anti-bribery policy upon approval from the Board as and when
required to prevent bribery and corruption in the Bank by persons associated with it and make
improvements as necessary from time to time.

deficiencies identified shall be rectified.

## 1.  Short Title& Definitions

## 1.1 Short Title and Commencement

This "Talent Hunt Guidelines" shallbe referred as "The Guideline" hereinafter.

 The contents of this guideline may be amended by the Boardas and when necessary.  This guideline (including  amendments  if  any)  shall  be  duly  communicated  to  the  concerned  staff  of  the  Bank.  Such amendments/alterations shall form an integral part of this guideline.

 Bank Management shall issue circulars/memorandums, as appropriate, to all staffs informing about "The Guideline".  All staff of the Bank must understand and be familiar with the contents of this guideline along with any amendments/alterations thereto.

 ## 1.2 Definition

Unless the subject or the context otherwise requires, in this Guideline,

- a) "The Bank" means Global IME Bank Limited.
 - b) 'The BOD' means Board of Directors.
 - c) "NRB" means Nepal Rastra Bank.
 - d) "BFIs" means a bank or financial institution which has obtained a license pursuant to Bank and Financial Institution Act 2073 BS for carrying on banking or financial transaction.
 - e) "CEO" means person appointed as the Chief Executive of the Bank, appointed by the Board and  entrusted  with  overall  Management,  Administration  and  Operations  of  the  Bank  and accountable to the Board.
 - f) "Staff" means staff of the Bank as defined in the HR By laws of the Bank.

 ## 2.  Introduction and Regulatory Requirement

## 2.1 Introduction

Human resources  are  the  most  important  resources  for  any  organization  and  this  becomes  even more important for the service industry like banking.  Experienced employees may not be available adequately  or  sometimes  experienced  employees  are  not  fulfilled  from  within  the  bank  or  from external vacancy announcement.  Hence, talent hunt is the best way to fulfill the requirement of staff in the bank whenever required.

 Talent hunt is a recruitment strategy of hiring best talents who are right fit for right type of job.  Talent hunt enables the bank to hire experienced candidates from the sources other than promotion, internal vacancy announcement and external vacancy announcement.

 ## 2.2 Regulatory Requirement

The Talent HuntGuideline has been developed in accordance with Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) Unified Directive No.  6.

 Bank Management shall issue circulars/memorandums, as appropriate, to all staffs informing about "The Guideline".  All staff of the Bank must understand and be familiar with the contents of this guideline along with any amendments/alterations thereto.

- a) "The Bank" means Global IME Bank Limited.
 - b) 'The BOD' means Board of Directors.

 - d) "BFIs" means a bank or financial institution which has obtained a license pursuant to Bank and Financial Institution Act 2073 BS for carrying on banking or financial transaction.

 Talent hunt is a recruitment strategy of hiring best talents who are right fit for right type of job.  Talent hunt enables the bank to hire experienced candidates from the sources other than promotion, internal vacancy announcement and external vacancy announcement.

The Talent HuntGuideline has been developed in accordance with Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) Unified Directive No.  6.

## 3.  Objective and Guiding Principles

## 3.1 Objectives of the guideline

Following are the key objectives of this guideline:

- a) To establish and enforce a transparent talent hunt practice.
 - b) To avoid confusion and ambiguity in recruitment of candidates under talent hunt and vacancy announcement.
 - c) To ensure availability of experienced manpower at all areas of the bank as and when necessary.
 - d) To fulfill suitable manpower in the bank in timely and cost effective manner.
 - e) To  fulfill the manpower  requirement created due to establishment of new  branches/ departments/subsidiaries as well as due to staff transfer and resignation.

 ## 3.2 Guiding Principles of the guideline

All Talent Hunt decisions shall be guided by following principles:

- a) Bank's need and requirement shall be the top priority in any talent hunt decision.
 - b) Recruitment under Talent Hunt shall be done within approved staff quota (Darbandi).
 - c) In general, the mode  of  selection  of candidates  shall be Interview.  However,  written examination, Group Discussion or any other practical examination, whenever required, can also be conducted while selecting candidates.
 - d) In order to fulfill the vacant positions, some candidates who were not selected previously need to be recalled for the second time.  Talent Hunt candidates can be recalled for selection process only after 2 months from the last interview date.
 - e) In order to appoint some candidates in certain positions, the remuneration of the bank may not be sufficient to them.  Hence, remuneration and facilities can be negotiated to compensate the Talent  Hunt  Candidates.   In  order  to  compensate  the  Talent  Hunt  Candidates,  the  Interview Panel can recommend additional grades and the same needs to be approved by Recruitment and Promotion Committee.
 - f) While appointing a candidate in certain position, he/she must fulfill minimum criteria as stated in  KarmachariSewaBiniyamawali,  2077  of  the  bank.   In  addition,  the  candidate  must  have minimum experience as mentioned in PPG in immediate lower position.
 - g) Talent  Hunt  shall  be  done  in  all  job  positions  except  in  Support  Level  Position,  Trainee Assistant and Management Trainee Positions.  However, in cases where requirement of Trainee Assistants  and  Management  Trainees  needs  to  be  fulfilled  via  College  Placement,  the recruitment can be considered under Talent Hunt.
 - h) For  any  issue  that  is  not  covered  herein,  the  talent  hunt  decisions  shall  be  guided  by KarmachariSewaBiniyamawali, 2077 of the bank.

## 3.1 Objectives of the guideline

Following are the key objectives of this guideline:

- a) To establish and enforce a transparent talent hunt practice.
 - b) To avoid confusion and ambiguity in recruitment of candidates under talent hunt and vacancy announcement.
 - c) To ensure availability of experienced manpower at all areas of the bank as and when necessary.
 - d) To fulfill suitable manpower in the bank in timely and cost effective manner.
 - e) To  fulfill the manpower  requirement created due to establishment of new  branches/ departments/subsidiaries as well as due to staff transfer and resignation.

 ## 3.2 Guiding Principles of the guideline

All Talent Hunt decisions shall be guided by following principles:

- a) Bank's need and requirement shall be the top priority in any talent hunt decision.
 - b) Recruitment under Talent Hunt shall be done within approved staff quota (Darbandi).
 - c) In general, the mode  of  selection  of candidates  shall be Interview.  However,  written examination, Group Discussion or any other practical examination, whenever required, can also be conducted while selecting candidates.
 - d) In order to fulfill the vacant positions, some candidates who were not selected previously need to be recalled for the second time.  Talent Hunt candidates can be recalled for selection process only after 2 months from the last interview date.
 - e) In order to appoint some candidates in certain positions, the remuneration of the bank may not be sufficient to them.  Hence, remuneration and facilities can be negotiated to compensate the Talent  Hunt  Candidates.   In  order  to  compensate  the  Talent  Hunt  Candidates,  the  Interview Panel can recommend additional grades and the same needs to be approved by Recruitment and Promotion Committee.
 - f) While appointing a candidate in certain position, he/she must fulfill minimum criteria as stated in  KarmachariSewaBiniyamawali,  2077  of  the  bank.   In  addition,  the  candidate  must  have minimum experience as mentioned in PPG in immediate lower position.
 - g) Talent  Hunt  shall  be  done  in  all  job  positions  except  in  Support  Level  Position,  Trainee Assistant and Management Trainee Positions.  However, in cases where requirement of Trainee Assistants  and  Management  Trainees  needs  to  be  fulfilled  via  College  Placement,  the recruitment can be considered under Talent Hunt.
 - h) For  any  issue  that  is  not  covered  herein,  the  talent  hunt  decisions  shall  be  guided  by KarmachariSewaBiniyamawali, 2077 of the bank.

## 1.  Correspondent Banking Definition

Correspondent Banking relationships are commonly used by banks internationally to undertake  financial  transactions  for  themselves  and  their  customers  in  jurisdictions where they generally have no physical presence.  A wide range of services can be settled through a correspondent banking relationship, including:

- a) Payments, including electronic transfers, drafts etc.
 - b) Buy / Sell of foreign exchanges
- c) Collections
- d) Placement of funds
- e) Trade finance transactions
- f) Counter Guarantees
- g) Remittances

Correspondent Banking relationships are established in two forms.  Other Banks and Financial Institutions (BFIs) may establish relationship with us (Vostro Account) and we may also need to establish relationship with local and international Banks (Nostro Account).

## 2.  Risks in Correspondent Banking

- 2.1 Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing: Correspondent banking relationships are exposed to money laundering and terrorism financing because they involve a bank carrying out financial transactions on behalf of another bank's customers.  On such indirect relationship we should depend on correspondent banks where our bank cannot verify the identities and obtain first-hand information about those customers.   If they do not undertake an appropriate level of initial and ongoing due diligence on such accounts, our  Bank may be exposed to risks associated with money laundering or terrorism financing.  'Layering' is a major risk the bank is exposed to and the Bank must be careful while selecting correspondent banking relationship.  It is the process by  depositing  money  in  one  bank  and  transferring  it  to  another  bank  in  the  same country or other country to convert the fund earned from illegal source to legal source.
 - 2.2 Reputational  Risk: Bank  has  a  risk  of  losing  its  reputation  by  unknowingly transacting funds originated from illegal activities if its correspondent bank fails to implement adequate or appropriate measures to prevent Money laundering or Terrorist Financing.
 - 2.3 Financial  Risk: Financially  weak  performance,  operational  failure  or  any  other unexpected event can cause bankruptcy of a correspondent bank which consequently results into financial loss to banks maintaining nostro account relation.
 - 2.4 Business  Risk: Correspondent  bank's  failure  to  execute  or  timely  execute  any transactions on behalf of the bank can hamper business or can cause financial/reputational loss to the bank.  Therefore, while choosing correspondent bank consideration of business reliability becomes very important.

 - 2.5 Country Risk: This risk may arise while maintaining fund in nostro account in the foreign country.  Massive changes in political system, change in regulated exchange rate  can  have  adverse  effects  on  business  of  a  correspondent  Bank.   Similarly, correspondent relationship is vulnerable to sovereign risk and transfer risk, which is the risk of capital being locked up or frozen by the government action.

metadata.author: Shishir Shakya
metadata.window:
## Mitigation and Measures

- a) Bank shall not establish any type (Nostro, Vostro or Relationship Management-RMA) of correspondent relationship with:
- i. Banks not having physical presence in any country (Shell bank) and any banks which carried out transactions with shell banks.
 - ii.  Unlicensed and/or unregulated financial institutions.
 - iii.  Any financial Institution and the country restricted by Nepal Rastra Bank or Government of Nepal or United Nations or any other internationally recognized authorities or local regulatory authority.
 - b) The  following  requirements  are  set  forth  for  establishing  Nostro  account relationship  and  Relationship  Management  (RMA)  with  any  banks  outside Nepal:
- i. Bank must have positive net worth to enter into correspondent relationship with Global IME Bank Ltd.
 - ii.  The bank should not be subject to sanctions, embargoes or similar measures issued  by  Nepal  or  United  Nations  or  FATF  or  any  other  internationally recognized authorities or local regulatory authority.
 - iii.  Correspondent Bank and International Bank must have minimum equivalent rating of B3/B- by any of renowned rating agency(ies), like Moody, Standard & Poor, and Fitch, etc.  In case of correspondent bank in India and other SAARC countries, local rating agencies may also be considered.  Localized ratings or implied ratings on Bloomberg/Reuters portal are also acceptable as long as they are similar or higher than B3/B- as mentioned above.  Banks appearing in the top 1000, Bankers' publications are also acceptable.
 - iv.  The maintenance of Nostro account relationship with any correspondent bank is subject to written approval from Nepal Rastra Bank which will be sufficient for the purpose of Due Diligence and documentation requirement.  ALCO shall set/review  the  credit  limit/ceiling  in  such  accounts.   A  credit  assessment  for Nostro Relationship is required and such is to be performed by the ALCO based on Treasury Department's recommendations.
 - v. Foreign Banks not meeting any one of the above criteria will be disqualified for establishing Nostro account relationship and Relationship Management (RMA).

## 3.  Responsibility

Treasury  Department,  which  is  currently  looking  after  Correspondent  Banking  shall ensure that proposed financial institution meets all the criteria set forth by the policy and obtain all the necessary documents before establishing correspondent relationships for Nostro account.  The department is also entrusted with the responsibility to update the information  on  periodic basis and  monitor  and  manage  relationships  with  the correspondent banks.

 ## 4.  Compliance/Audit

Compliance and Audit Department will have the responsibility of reviewing correspondent  banking  documents  and  processes  on  periodic  basis  to  ensure  the fulfillment of the requirement sent forth by the policy.

 ## 5.  Miscellaneous

- i. This policy shall be reviewed whenever it is deemed necessary.
 - ii.  This policy, and amendment thereto, shall come into effect from the date of approval by the Board of Directors of the Bank.

## Unified Branch Operations Manual

Reviewed on: April 2024

<!-- image -->

## Preamble

In order to manage the branch operations of Global IME Bank Ltd., the Chief Executive Officer of the Bank has approved this Unified Branch Operations Manual and it shall come into immediate effect after country circular is issued.

 This manual-guideline has been developed in order to streamline the operations procedures in relation to  branch  operations  and  related  transactional  procedures  in  Global  IME  Bank  Ltd  (GIBL).   This document  covers  the  branch  operations  manual  for  Customer  Service  Department,  Cash,  Vault Operations and Transaction Procedures, Outward Remittance and Safe Deposit Locker (Vault).

## CHAPTER 1 CUSTOMER SERVICE DEPARTMENT-OPERATIONS MANUAL

## 1.1 Definition of Terms

## 1.1.1 Customer

A customer is anyone who want to use or is user of a product or service offered by the bank.  The customer can be new or existing/repeat customer.

 ## 1.1.2 Deposit Account

An account that allows money to be deposited and withdrawn by an account holder based on different terms and features offered by the bank where deposits are maintained.

 ## 1.1.3 Foreign Currency Account

A deposit account opened in convertible foreign currency i.e.  any currency except Nepalese Rupees and Indian Rupees.

 ## 1.1.4 Account Statement

A document with list of all transactions performed in a bank account over a set period of time.

 ## 1.1.5 Standing Instruction

Instruction  to  the  bank  from  a  customer  about  actions  to  be  taken  under  fulfillment  of  required conditions as mentioned in the documents.

 ## 1.1.6 Stop Payment

An instruction made for stopping payment against cheque at the request of account holder.

 ## 1.1.7 Balance Certificate

A certificate issued by the bank, on request made by the account holder, showing the balance present in the account maintained at the bank.

 ## 1.1.8 Dormant Account

Dormant account is the status of an account which indicates that there has been no customer-initiated transaction in the account for a certain period of time.  As per the NRB Directive, accounts having no transactions for at least last three years in case of savings accounts and last one year in case of current and call accounts are to be categorized as dormant accounts.  Such accounts are restricted for any kind of customer induced debit transaction.

 ## 1.1.9 Foreign Currency

All  cash,  notes  and  metal  coins,  which  are  issued  by  foreign  country.   Foreign  currency  is  further classified as convertible and non-convertible currency:

-  Non-convertible currency: Indian currency is not convertible to any other currency other than Nepalese Rupees.

 <!-- image -->

-  Convertible  currency: All  other  foreign  currencies  whose  buying  and  selling  rates  are published by NRB.

 ## 1.1.10 Illiterate Person

One who cannot read or write.  A person who cannot sign or who makes thumb impression for opening bank account and carrying out other banking transactions is regarded as illiterate for the purpose of opening account in the bank.

## 1.1.11 Minor

Person below the age of 18 years.

 ## 1.1.12 Mandatee

A person receiving mandate/power of attorney (authorization) to operate the account on behalf of the account holder is referred for this purpose as Mandatee.

 ## 1.1.13 Debit Card

An instrument of payment that can be used in place of cash and cash items in form of plastic cards in which account of the customer is debited in the real time while performing the transaction.

 ## 1.1.14 Operations In-Charge

A staff who is assigned and authorized to supervise, facilitate and approve all the activities in the cash and operations area in the branch.  He/she is the head of the department in the branch and is accountable to the activities of overall branch operations including customer service.

 ## 1.1.15 Vault Key Holder

A staff who is assigned and authorized custodian to hold and handle the bank's vault/locker/strong room/fire-proof cabinet etc.  as assigned by the Branch Manager.  He/she is responsible for the movement of cash or any other items from/to the vault.

 ## 1.1.16 Beneficial Owner

A natural person who ultimately owns or controls an account on whose behalf transactions are being conducted.  Likewise, it also includes a natural person who exercises effective control over a legal entity.

 ## 1.1.17 Risk Appetite

Risk appetite refers to an organization's predetermined level of tolerance or willingness to accept and manage operational risks.  It outlines the boundaries within which an organization is willing to operate while considering the potential negative impacts of various operational risks, such as errors, system failures, fraud, or legal issues.

 ## 1.2 Savings and Transactional Accounts Operational Procedure

Deposit refers to any sum of money deposited by the customer with the bank with feature of interest bearing or non-interest bearing as per types of deposit product.  Deposit is a liability owed by a bank to the account holder.  The bank account holder has the right to withdraw entirely or partially the deposited funds as per the stated terms and conditions and features of the deposit products.

 <!-- image -->

metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## Types of deposit:

- a. Current: An account maintained for transactional purpose and does not earn any interest.  Any amount deposited in this account is available on demand.  However, the minimum balance as per the account scheme should be maintained.  This account is generally targeted to the business entities and institutions which require operating through a bank for their daily transactions.
 - b. Savings: A deposit account maintained with the bank by an individual or non-profit making entities for savings purpose with feature of earning some interests on the deposits made in the account.  Such deposit may or may not have a minimum balance depending on the types and features of the deposit product.
 - c. Call: A deposit account which is normally opened by business entities and other institutions in order to make their deposits smarter.  This account yields some interest.
 - d. Fixed: A deposit account opened for a fixed term with the understanding that the account holder can  withdraw  the  fund  only  after  maturity  of  the  deposit.   It  is  opened  with  the  purpose  of savings in which rate of interest is generally higher than other types of deposit and has a specific date of maturity.

metadata.title: Unified Branch Operations Manual
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 1.2.1 Procedure for Opening an Account

- A. The completely filled Account Opening Form (AOF) should be obtained from the customer at the  time  of  opening  the  account  except  in  cases  where  it  is  separately  governed  by  Bank's policy/ Government Policy.
 - The Account Opening Form must be completely filled by the customer.  However, the customer can be guided to complete the form properly.  The customer must be briefly stated about the terms and conditions with regard to opening and operation of the account.  Branch needs to obtain signature of the customer at the end of the terms and conditions as an acknowledgement of acceptance of the terms and conditions.
 - B. The  customer  must  be  self-present  in  the  branch  and,  or  sign  the  Account  Opening  Form/ Signature Specimen Card in front of the staff or any concerned bank official.  Customers may opt  for  video  KYC  solution  provided  by  the  bank  for  customer  verification  to  open  bank account.
 - C. The staff at CSD shall ensure that the Account Opening Form is completely filled up and all related documents as per annexure of AML/CFT Guidelines are obtained.  The customer needs to present original documents at the time of opening the account and copies of all documents should be verified with original.  A notarized copy documents can be accepted duly attested by notary public.  The staff of Customer Service Department needs to endorse 'Verified with True Copy' stamp in copies of all the documents submitted.
 - D. In case of documents/AOF or other applications received by other branches, staff or foreign representative offices, it is the responsibility of receiving branch or office to verify the original documents, signatures, person being present or any other type of verification and forward the same to concerned home branch for further processing.  The staff making such verification should  sign  the  documents  along  with  Staff  ID  and  confirm  the  presence  of  the  person  / applicant  through  email.   The  documents  which  are  verified  needs  to  be  forwarded  through BM/OI of other branch or from representative office to the concerned BM/OI of home branch.
 - E. In  case  of  personal  accounts  (including  joint  personal  accounts  and  sole  proprietorship accounts) complete details of the nominee as required in the Account Opening Form should be obtained if the customer wants to keep nominee in the account.  In case the customer does not want to appoint nominee, the section of nominee in Account Opening Form must be crossed.

- F. A recent photograph of the account holder, account operator must be kept in the AOF and/or Signature Specimen Card and should be scanned along with specimen signature in the system. - b. Short name - first name of the customer in full

- e. Passport number and expiry date
- f. Date of birth - as mentioned in birth certificate (in case of minor) or citizenship certificate/passport

- h. PAN Type - permanent or temporary
- i. Current Address - residential address
- j. Permanent Address - as mentioned in citizenship certificate
- k. Customer Risk Grading - in line with the directive of NRB / AML/CFT Guidelines of the Bank
- l. Type - type of customer
- m. Instruction of account operations
- n. Screening ID - as generated from sanction screening software etc.

metadata.title: Unified Branch Operations Manual
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 1.2.2 Opening of Foreign Currency Account

Foreign currency account can be opened in convertible foreign currency listed in the bank's foreign exchange list having both buying and selling rate.  All the saving, current, call and fixed deposit accounts can be opened in foreign currency.

 Opening of foreign currency account is subject to the provisions made in circulars and directives issued by Nepal Rastra Bank from time to time.  Due attention should be paid in regard to foreign exchange regulation of Nepal Rastra Bank while opening account in foreign currency.  Necessary documents as required by NRB guidelines for opening of account in foreign currency must be obtained at the time of opening of the account.

 - A. Individual person and/or firm, company having source of income in foreign currency can open a FCY account.  Similarly, companies carrying out foreign currency transactions, like; hotels, airlines,  travel  &  trekking  agents,  moneychanger,  remittance  companies  can  open  a  FCY account upon approval from Nepal Rastra Bank.
 - Branch needs to obtain documents evidencing source of income in foreign currency.
 - B. FCY accounts opened in the name of firm/company on the basis of NRB Permit can be operated till the validity of the NRB permit.  The firm/company needs to submit renewed copy of the permit after expiry within stipulated time period as per the NRB directives.
 - In case the customer fails to submit the renewed copy of NRB permit within stipulated period of time including grace period of 30 days or as per the NRB circular, branch shall ensure that the account has been total freeze by the system till the required renewed copy is submitted by the account holder.
 - In case of foreign nationals, the account opened by the foreign individual can be operated till the validity of the visa of the account holder.  If the account holder fails to submit valid visa or extension of visa, branch shall mark total freeze in the account till the account holder submits the copy of visa extension to the branch.
 - C. While opening foreign currency account, the provisions made in directives issued by Nepal Rastra Bank from time to time needs to be adhered too.  The provisions regarding operation of the account, FCY cash deposit in the account, withdrawal from the account, fund transfer, FCY exchange facilities to the FCY account holders should be followed.

__data__.text:
- In case the customer fails to submit the renewed copy of NRB permit within stipulated period of time including grace period of 30 days or as per the NRB circular, branch shall ensure that the account has been total freeze by the system till the required renewed copy is submitted by the account holder.
 - In case of foreign nationals, the account opened by the foreign individual can be operated till the validity of the visa of the account holder.  If the account holder fails to submit valid visa or extension of visa, branch shall mark total freeze in the account till the account holder submits the copy of visa extension to the branch.
 - C. While opening foreign currency account, the provisions made in directives issued by Nepal Rastra Bank from time to time needs to be adhered too.  The provisions regarding operation of the account, FCY cash deposit in the account, withdrawal from the account, fund transfer, FCY exchange facilities to the FCY account holders should be followed.

## 1.2.3 Account of Illiterate Person/Disabled Person

- A. A person who is illiterate or is disabled to read and write can open and operate the account with his/her thumb impression.  Illiterate person includes those who cannot read and write on their own.  Disabled person includes visually impaired, mentally challenged, and having disabilities that  limits  the  person  to  operate  the  account  independently  without  help/support  of  legal guardian.
 - B. Thumb  Impression  of  both  right  and  left  hand  should  be  clearly  obtained  in  the  Account Opening Form and Signature Specimen Card.  The Thumb Impression must be obtained in the presence of the staff of the bank.
 - C. Branch  shall  obtain  recent  photograph(s)  of  the  customer  and  attach  a  photograph  in  the Signature Specimen Card.  Photograph of the customer should be scanned in the system.
 - D. The account with thumb impression should be operated in the presence of the account holder him/herself.   The  account  holder  must  be  present  in  the  bank  along  with  identification documents for withdrawal transaction.  Staff at the counter shall attest the thumb impression

<!-- image -->

only after confirming and verifying with the photograph and identification documents in the record of the branch and proceed for payment of the cheque.

 - E. An illiterate person with thumb impression for account operation cannot open a joint account.
 - F. An illiterate person with thumb impression for account operation cannot appoint a mandatee.
 - G. Mentally challenged person(s) are also entitled to open account with the bank.  The account shall be operated by the parent(s)/legal guardian of the account holder.
 - H. Account of differently abled person can be opened.  The customer should be briefed about the process of account opening and other applicable terms in presence of a witness (as deemed necessary).

metadata.title: Unified Branch Operations Manual
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 1.2.4 Account of Minor

- A. A person under the age of 18 is termed as minor.  The account of a minor should be opened in the minor's name with the parents or legal guardian as the account operator.  The account shall be operated by the parents or legal guardian till the minor attains majority.
 - B. The account opening request must be made by the parents or the legal guardian.  For opening of a minor account, following documents must be obtained:
- a. Birth registration certificate or minor registration certificate issued by concerned Government Authority.
 - b. Citizenship certificate and guardianship certificate in case of account open request by legal guardian
- c. Recent photograph of the minor, parents and/or legal guardians
- C.  "MINOR" remarks should be marked in the Account Opening Form.  Date of attaining majority of the minor should be mentioned in the Account Opening Form and system.  Details of minority of the account holder must be inserted in CBS.
 - D. Unless  and  until  prohibited  by  any  legal/special  instruction,  the  parent/legal  guardian  is authorized to operate the minor account.  Once the minor becomes major the account should be immediately  blocked  for  withdrawal  transactions  i.e.   Debit  Freeze.   The  account  holder, parent/legal guardians should be informed and requested to submit necessary documents for operation of the account as a normal account by the account holder.  Early information is to be provided  to  parent/legal  guardian  for  necessary  documents  preferably  a  month  prior  to  the majority date.  A new account opening form should be filled for operations of the account by the minor who has turned into major.
 - E. In  case  any  other  person,  other  than  parents  are  going  to  operate  the  minor  account, guardianship certificate issued by the court is required.
 - On majority, the account holder is entitled to operate the account as a regular account (instead of minor account).  A written request of the parent/legal guardian and the account holder should be obtained accordingly to change the mode of account operation.  Identification documents (citizenship certificate) of the account holder should be obtained and updated in the account opening file.

 All remarks noted to indicate minor account should be removed in the system.

 The account of minor may be closed at the request of the parents or legal guardians.  However, if the minor has already turned into major, his/her consent shall also be required to close the account.

 - B. The account opening request must be made by the parents or the legal guardian.  For opening of a minor account, following documents must be obtained:
- a. Birth registration certificate or minor registration certificate issued by concerned Government Authority.
 - b. Citizenship certificate and guardianship certificate in case of account open request by legal guardian
- c. Recent photograph of the minor, parents and/or legal guardians
- C.  "MINOR" remarks should be marked in the Account Opening Form.  Date of attaining majority of the minor should be mentioned in the Account Opening Form and system.  Details of minority of the account holder must be inserted in CBS.
 - D. Unless  and  until  prohibited  by  any  legal/special  instruction,  the  parent/legal  guardian  is authorized to operate the minor account.  Once the minor becomes major the account should be immediately  blocked  for  withdrawal  transactions  i.e.   Debit  Freeze.   The  account  holder, parent/legal guardians should be informed and requested to submit necessary documents for operation of the account as a normal account by the account holder.  Early information is to be provided  to  parent/legal  guardian  for  necessary  documents  preferably  a  month  prior  to  the majority date.  A new account opening form should be filled for operations of the account by the minor who has turned into major.
 - E. In  case  any  other  person,  other  than  parents  are  going  to  operate  the  minor  account, guardianship certificate issued by the court is required.
 - On majority, the account holder is entitled to operate the account as a regular account (instead of minor account).  A written request of the parent/legal guardian and the account holder should be obtained accordingly to change the mode of account operation.  Identification documents (citizenship certificate) of the account holder should be obtained and updated in the account opening file.

 All remarks noted to indicate minor account should be removed in the system.

 The account of minor may be closed at the request of the parents or legal guardians.  However, if the minor has already turned into major, his/her consent shall also be required to close the account.

metadata.title: Unified Branch Operations Manual
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 1.2.6 Refusal to Open an Account

The decision to open an account for a new customer creates a strong legal relationship between the customer  and  the  bank.   Hence,  it  is  the  primary  responsibility  of  the  branch  to  carry  out  rigorous examination and verification of documents and customer information prior to opening of a new account.  All new customers should correctly complete the relevant account opening documents and furnish all supporting documents as required by AML/CFT Guidelines of the bank.

 Branch shall verify the copies of documents submitted and information provided by the customer for opening of a new account.  The right to refuse to open an account rests upon Operations Incharge or Branch Manager.

 - A. Branch shall not open the account, if the customer denies providing all details in the Account Opening Form or providing information as required by Customer Due Diligence or submission of any documents.  Account should also not to be opened if the information provided by the customer seems suspicious.
 - B. Branch shall not open any account without complete KYC documents and/or KYC information.  Account without complete  documents if presented, the  branch  may  open  the  account  upon written consent of BM to complete the documentation within 7 working days from the date of the account opened.  Branch shall not issue cheque book, card or any other withdrawal facility to the account and shall restrict for any withdrawal transactions in the account immediately till all the required documents are submitted by the customer.

 All the documents related to such account should be kept in a separate file in the branch.

 Staff at CSD shall maintain a record of all such accounts with incomplete documents, which should be reviewed on periodical basis.  Regular follow up should be made for completion of documents and written communication should be made to the customer to submit required documents.   On  submission  of  all  required  documents,  the  account  should  be  updated  and treated as a normal account.

 - C. Branch should not open Savings Account to any other customer, except for natural persons and organizations established with nonprofit objectives.

 <!-- image -->

- D. Staff of the Bank should not be allowed to open any other accounts in any branches except the account opened upon recommendation from Human Resource Department for the purpose of salary deposit and payment, loan facility etc.
 - E. Branch should comply with NRB directive related to multiple account opening of individual.

 In case of institution, more than one operative or non-operative account can be opened provided that the purpose of opening the account is clear.

 However, branch must ensure that the multiple accounts are opened with the same Client ID Number in the system.

## 1.2.7 Safekeeping of Account Opening Forms and Related Documents

- A. Branch shall maintain a separate file for each account opened in the branch.   All documents related to account opening and further correspondences, waivers, approvals etc.  related to the customer must be kept in the respective file.
 - B. Branch shall keep all the account opening files in chronological series according to the account number assigned.  The account opening documents must be kept safely in closed cabinet or any other storage ensuring proper security.  It should also be ensured that Account Opening forms can be retrieved promptly as and when needed.
 - C. All documents maintained in the file of the customer should be scanned and uploaded in the Intranet (E-kagaj) on the same day the account is opened or by next working day if the scan is not completed due to any technical reason or unavoidable circumstances.

metadata.title: Unified Branch Operations Manual
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 1.2.8 Mandate

Personal  account  holder  and  sole  proprietorship  account  holder  can  authorize  any  other  person  to operate the account on behalf of the account holder.  The person authorized to operate the account, also called as mandatee, is authorized to operate the account.  The account holder can appoint more than one mandatee in the account.  However, the mandatee is not authorized to appoint another mandatee or cancel signature of the account holder or close the account.

 - A. Branch shall obtain a mandate form as per standard format, copy of citizenship and photograph of mandatee.  The citizenship certificate must be duly verified with the original.  Due diligence along with screening of the mandatee should be carried out as per AML/CFT guidelines of the bank.
 - B. Both  the  accountholder(s)  and  the  mandatee  must  be  present  in  the  Bank  and,  or  sign  the documents in front of the bank staff or appropriate authority of the Bank.  Once the mandatee has been appointed, the signature of the mandatee must be uploaded in the system along with signature remarks for mode of account operation.
 - C. Individual account operated by mandate who is not the family member of account holder shall be categorized as high risk.  Approval from COCO/COO should be taken for such cases.
 - D. In  the  presence  of  the  accountholder(s),  the  person  receiving  the  mandate  must  be  clearly explained about the authority that has been delegated by the accountholder(s).  The mandatee shall be authorized only to:
- a. Carry out financial transaction in the account
- b. Request  for  cheque  book,  ATM/debit  card,  e-banking  and  other  facilities  as specifically requested by the accountholder

<!-- image -->

- c. Request for stop payment
- d. Receive correspondence on behalf of the accountholder's
- e. Request for other service related to the account operation,
- E. The right of mandatee can be cancelled upon receipt of written request by the accountholder(s).  Branch shall  remove  the  signature  of  the  mandatee  from  the  system  for  account  operation immediately upon receipt of the cancellation request of the accountholder(s).

## 1.2.8 Mandate

Personal  account  holder  and  sole  proprietorship  account  holder  can  authorize  any  other  person  to operate the account on behalf of the account holder.  The person authorized to operate the account, also called as mandatee, is authorized to operate the account.  The account holder can appoint more than one mandatee in the account.  However, the mandatee is not authorized to appoint another mandatee or cancel signature of the account holder or close the account.

## 1.2.9 Issuance of Cheque Book

## 1.2.9.1 Maintenance of Cheque

General Service Department (GSD) shall be responsible for procurement of cheque and delivery to the concerned branches as per their requirements raised by the branches.

 - A. The stock of cheque in a branch must be kept safely in the vault room.  Branch shall maintain a cheque stock register as per standard format to record the details containing date of receipt, cheque serial number, quantity, balance.  The register must be updated each time the stock is kept in or out the vault   along with the signature of the concerned staff.
 - B. The vault custodian shall provide only the necessary quantity of cheque to the staff of Customer Service Department for daily requirement.  At the end of the day, the departmental stock of cheque for daily use must be kept in the vault room/fire proof cabinet overnight.
 - On daily basis, the vault custodians shall verify issuance and remaining stock as per the record kept in the department.
 - In case if any staff is going on leave or transferred or has resigned, the staff holding the stock of Cheque must transfer the stock to the alternate staff in Customer Service Department.  The stock in Core Banking system must be transferred to the alternate staff and the stock transfer details should be recorded in the Department Stock register .
 - C. Branch shall record the cheque stock in the system as follows:
- a. Total stock received from GSD
- b. Total number of cheques handed over to CSD for departmental requirement on daily basis.

 Each time the cheque stock is received from GSD or handed over to the staff at CSD for daily use, the details of cheque stock must be recorded in the system.

metadata.window:
## 1.2.9.2 Issuance of Cheque against Cheque Requisition Slip

- A. Cheque book should be issued on the  basis of "Request for Cheque Book" in case of new account and "Cheque Book Requisition Slip" in case of existing account.  Cheque book should be  issued  after  confirming  that  the  minimum  balance  is  maintained  in  the  account  and  the signature of the account holder in the Cheque Request/Requisition Slip is verified.
 - B. Cheque Book of other branches shall require the approval of BM.  The issuing branch should ensure that KYC of the account holder is fully updated before issuance of the cheque book.  The issuing  branch  can  confirm  KYC  update  status  by  checking  documents  in  E-Kagaj/DMS.  Cheque requisition slip should be kept in the record of the issuing branch itself.
 - C. Cheque book should be system printed.
 - D. At  the  time  of  issuance,  following  details  must  be  written  in  the  rear  side  of  the  Cheque Requisition Slip along with round stamp of the branch:
- a. Date of issuance
- b. Name of the account holder
- c. Account number
- d. Cheque serial number issued (from ……….  to ……………)
- e. Full signature of the staff who prepares the cheque book
- f. Staff ID number
- E. For each cheque book only one leaf of Cheque Book Requisition Slip should be attached inside the cheque book.  The serial number of Cheque Requisition Slip must be recorded in the Cheque Book Issue Register.
 - F. For next issuance of cheque book, branch shall obtain the Cheque Requisition Slip and verify the authenticity of the request.  The details mentioned in requisition slip must be checked and verified  along  with  the  signature  of  the  account  holder.     The  serial  number  of  Cheque Requisition Slip must be recorded in the Cheque Book Issue Register.
 - G. Prior to issuance of the cheque book, branch needs to check the status of earlier cheques in the system.  If it appears that many previously issued cheques are still unused, then the customer must be inquired about the need for fresh cheques and forward the request to the Operations InCharge.  New cheque book should be issued after the Operations In-Charge is satisfied with the genuineness and requirement of the customer's request.

Cheque book should be  issued  after  confirming  that  the  minimum  balance  is  maintained  in  the  account  and  the signature of the account holder in the Cheque Request/Requisition Slip is verified.
 - B. Cheque Book of other branches shall require the approval of BM.  The issuing branch should ensure that KYC of the account holder is fully updated before issuance of the cheque book.  The issuing  branch  can  confirm  KYC  update  status  by  checking  documents  in  E-Kagaj/DMS.  Cheque requisition slip should be kept in the record of the issuing branch itself.
 - C. Cheque book should be system printed.
 - D. At  the  time  of  issuance,  following  details  must  be  written  in  the  rear  side  of  the  Cheque Requisition Slip along with round stamp of the branch:
- a. Date of issuance
- b. Name of the account holder
- c. Account number
- d. Cheque serial number issued (from ……….  to ……………)
- e. Full signature of the staff who prepares the cheque book
- f. Staff ID number
- E. For each cheque book only one leaf of Cheque Book Requisition Slip should be attached inside the cheque book.  The serial number of Cheque Requisition Slip must be recorded in the Cheque Book Issue Register.
 - F. For next issuance of cheque book, branch shall obtain the Cheque Requisition Slip and verify the authenticity of the request.  The details mentioned in requisition slip must be checked and verified  along  with  the  signature  of  the  account  holder.     The  serial  number  of  Cheque Requisition Slip must be recorded in the Cheque Book Issue Register.
 - G. Prior to issuance of the cheque book, branch needs to check the status of earlier cheques in the system.  If it appears that many previously issued cheques are still unused, then the customer must be inquired about the need for fresh cheques and forward the request to the Operations InCharge.  New cheque book should be issued after the Operations In-Charge is satisfied with the genuineness and requirement of the customer's request.

- K. Cheque  book  can  be  collected  by  the  accountholder  or  by  the  authorized  agent  of  the accountholder mentioned in the cheque requisition slip.  For the cases where the accounts have been  opened  in  large  numbers  for  specific  purpose  like  salary  or  distribution  of  funds  the cheques can be handed over to the concerned RM / Staff handling such  relationship-based approval.  Concerned staff shall submit the documentary evidence of delivery of such cheque to concerned accountholder or agent.
 - L. Signature of the account holder must be obtained in the register and verified on delivery of the cheque book.  In case the cheque is to be handed over to an authorized agent, the signature of the authorized agent must be obtained in the register and verified with specimen provided on the requisition slip.  A copy of identification documents of the authorized agent must be attached with the requisition slip.  Prior to delivery of the cheque book, signature of the received/authorized agent in the requisition slip as well as in cheque issuance register must be verified.
 - M. Illiterate  persons  with Thumb  Impression for account operation cannot appoint an agent to collect cheque on their behalf.  The account holder must be present in the bank for issuance of the cheque book.
 - N. The  staff  at  CSD  issuing/delivering  the  cheque  book  to  the  customer  must  mark  his/her signature in the Cheque Book Issuance Register on delivery of the cheque book to the customer.
 - O. After the cheque book is issued, the customer must be asked to check and count the number of leaves to ascertain that the cheque book and number of leaves have been correctly provided.
 - P. After the cheque book is delivered to the customer, all related documents including cheque request  letter,  cheque  requisition  slip,  authorization  letter,  identification  document  of  the accountholder and/or agent must be kept in the record of the issuing branch.
 - Q. Operations In-charge shall check the Cheque Book Issuance register on daily basis to check and verify the correctness of cheque book issuance and acknowledgement by the customer on delivery.

 - M. Illiterate  persons  with Thumb  Impression for account operation cannot appoint an agent to collect cheque on their behalf.  The account holder must be present in the bank for issuance of the cheque book.
 - N. The  staff  at  CSD  issuing/delivering  the  cheque  book  to  the  customer  must  mark  his/her signature in the Cheque Book Issuance Register on delivery of the cheque book to the customer.

__data__.text:
- O. After the cheque book is issued, the customer must be asked to check and count the number of leaves to ascertain that the cheque book and number of leaves have been correctly provided.
 - P. After the cheque book is delivered to the customer, all related documents including cheque request  letter,  cheque  requisition  slip,  authorization  letter,  identification  document  of  the accountholder and/or agent must be kept in the record of the issuing branch.
 - Q. Operations In-charge shall check the Cheque Book Issuance register on daily basis to check and verify the correctness of cheque book issuance and acknowledgement by the customer on delivery.

## 1.2.9.3 Issuance of Cheque without Cheque Requisition Slip

In absence of the Cheque Requisition Slip, staff at CSD must take extra precaution for issuance of new cheque book to avoid any possible instance of unauthorized issuance of cheque.  There may be different reasons for non- presentment of the requisition slip like due to loss of cheque book or requisition slip.

 - A. In  case  of  personal  accounts,  the  account  holder  or  the  mandatee  must  submit  a  written request/bank standard application for issuing fresh cheque book with the reason for not being able to submit the Cheque Requisition Slip.  The cheque book must be issued only after the verification of the signature in the request letter.
 - B. In case of account of entity, the request must be made in written by the authorized signatories along with the seal of the company.  The request letter must contain the specimen signature of the  authorized  agent  to  collect  the  cheque  book.   Branch  shall  obtain  photo  identification documents of the authorized agent.
 - The authorized signatories should also be confirmed over the phone/email if deemed necessary.  The  date,  time,  contact  number  or  email  correspondence  of  confirmation  with  the  account holder must be noted or attached in the request letter.
 - C. If  non-submission  of  cheque  book  requisition  slip  is  due  to  loss  of  the  cheque  book,  the customer should be advised to stop the unused cheque leaves as per record in the system.   On written request of the customer, branch shall mark stop payment of the unused cheque(s) in the system.

 <!-- image -->

- D. Branch shall recover applicable charges while issuing the cheque without obtaining cheque requisition slip.

## 1.2.9.4 Uncollected Cheque Book

Cheque book prepared but not collected by customer for three months or more shall be referred as Uncollected Cheque Book.

 - A. Branch  shall  keep  all  uncollected  cheque  books  in  Customer  Service  Department  during transaction hour for delivery/providing to the customers.  If the cheque books are not collected by the customer during the transaction hour, then such undelivered cheque book should be kept in fire proof cabinet/vault overnight under joint custody of staff in CSD or vault custodians.  Daily reconciliation of all uncollected cheque book should be done by CSD staff/staff assigned by the BM/OI.
 - B. On monthly basis branch shall segregate uncollected cheque books not collected for a period of  more  than  three  months.   These  cheque  books  must  be  kept  separately  in  a  fire  proof cabinet/vault under the joint custody of staff in CSD or vault custodians.

 An inventory of uncollected cheque books must be maintained at the branch and updated on daily basis.  The record should contain following details:

- a. Account Number
- b. Account name
- c. Cheque Serial Number (from … to …)
- d. Number of leaves printed
- e. Cheque Requisition Slip and Slip No.  (if any)
- f. Cheque printed date

In case of uncollected cheques printed by other branches, it is the responsibility of the printing branch to destroy such cheques by following the required process and notifying the concerned home branch.

 Branch shall take the uncollected cheuqe book out of the vault/fire proof cabinet only in case the customer visits to collect the cheque book.  The register of the uncollected cheque book should be updated each time the cheque is delivered to/collected by the customer.

metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
Branch shall follow following process to destroy the uncollected cheque books:

<!-- image -->

- a. Branch shall segregate the cheque books not collected for more than one year and tally the number of physical cheque books with the record.
 - b. Branch shall forward the detail of uncollected cheque books to respective Province Office and  obtain  approval  from  concerned  authority  as  per  Operational  Approving  Authority Matrix for disposal of uncollected cheque books.
 - c. Upon approval, Operations In-Charge shall review and check the list of uncollected cheque books  to  confirm  the  total  count  and  eligibility  for  disposal.   Branch  shall  destroy uncollected cheque books in the presence of following staff:
- i. Staff from Customer Service Department
- ii.  Operations In-Charge
- iii.  Branch Manager
- d. Before disposal of cheque, the branch should ensure that:
- i. Customer's  statement  of  account  has  been  checked  to  ensure  that  the movement of account justifies the disposal of cheque book.
 - ii.  The customer has been contacted over phone/email and reason(s) for noncollection has been noted.
 - iii.  If the  customer  could  not  be  contacted,  the  call  reports  have  been maintained in the record.
 - e. Branch shall collect necessary charge if applicable, as per standard tariff of fees and charges of the bank.
 - f. The  cheque  book  should  be  destroyed  preferably  by  shredding  or  by  incinerating  the cheques at a safe and secured place.
 - g. The inventory of cheques in customer's account in the system should also be marked as destroyed/cancelled  upon  physical  destruction.   Similarly,  the  list  of  cheque  books destroyed must be marked as "Destroyed" in the Uncollected Cheque Book Inventory and Cheque Book Issuance Register.
 - h. A record of disposal of uncollected cheques must be prepared and signed by all staff present at the time of disposal.  The record must contain following details:
-  Account Number
-  Account Name
-  Cheque Serial Number (from … to …)
-  Number of Leaves printed
-  Date of Cheque Destruction
-  Date of Approval
-  Reason(s) for Destruction if any
-  Method and Location of Destruction
- i. Branch shall keep the record of cheque destruction for future reference.

## 1.2.9.5 Issuance of Cheque Book in Call Accounts

Cheque  book  should  not  be  issued  in  any  type  of  call  accounts.   For  existing  customers  having maintained call accounts where if any cheque book has been issued earlier, no new cheque shall be provided on next requisition.  The client should be provided with cheque book for savings and/or current account only.
