## 3.2.2 Telegraphic Transfer (TT)

## 3.2.2.1 Telegraphic Transfer for Outward Remittance

- A. The applicant should be account holder of the bank for issuance of TT.  For payment of some services like fees for college, medical treatment and similar nature, the transaction may be done through account of parent/guardian/dependent upon obtaining the document evidencing relationship and identification of the applicant.
 - B. The applicant should fill the standard form of the bank.   The application should be prepared in two copies and should contain:
- a. Full name and address of applicant
- b. Purpose of the transfer
- c. Currency and amount to be transferred in words and figures

- d. Full name and address of beneficiary and if available the account number and telephone number of the beneficiary
- C. Branch shall obtain the amount to be remitted along with the applicable commission and SWIFT charge from the customer.  All applicable charges are to be obtained in accordance with the schedule of fees and charges of the bank.  The total amount can be received debiting the customer's account.
 - D. Branch shall make entry of TT transaction and SWIFT message in the CBS.  Record the detail of SWIFT message in a register.  Branch shall mention the Tran ID, reference number and details  of  amount  transferred  and  commission  charged  to  the  customer  in  the  SWIFT application form.  The customer copy of the application form duly signed and marked with bank stamp should be provided to the customer/applicant.
 - E. The SWIFT message should be signed by two authorized persons as per the signing authority mentioned in List of Authorized Signatures of the Bank.  The signed SWIFT message should be forwarded to SWIFT Department within the stipulated time.
 - F. SWIFT Department on receipt of branch request, shall route the message and forward a copy of SWIFT message to the concerned branch.
 - G. After the SWIFT transmitted copy is received from SWIFT Department, branch should check and verify whether the correct message was transmitted so that the error can be rectified in time  without  any  delay.   The  copy  of  SWIFT  message  should  be  kept  along  with  the application and documents in the file.
 - H. It shall be responsibility of the requesting branch to make the follow up with Swift Operations for transmitted copy of the message to keep in the branch record.
 - I. Treasury  Department  should  be  pre-informed  before  transfer  of  the  SWIFT  message  for purpose of necessary fund arrangement in Nostro.
 - J. While transferring foreign currency, the directives issued by Nepal Rastra Bank from time to time should be adhered to.  While remitting the fund through SWIFT in foreign currency, following procedures are to be followed:
- a. The amount to be transferred and the purpose of such transfer should be in accordance with the directive issued by Nepal Rastra Bank from time to time.
 - b. All required documents as per the directive of Nepal Rastra Bank should be obtained.
 - c. In  case  of  transfer  of  foreign  currency  equivalent  to  over  USD  1,000.00,  foreign currency exchange rate should be obtained from Treasury Department.
 - K. Issuance of TT facility for import related transactions should be allowed only to the account holders of the bank.

## 3.2.2.2 Issuance of TT for Import of Goods from India/third country

Similar provisions as mentioned in 3.2.1.3 shall be followed in relation to issuance of TT for import of goods from India.

 ## 3.2.2.3 Cancellation of TT

- A. The applicant should submit a written request to cancel the TT.  The signature of the applicant should be verified with the signature in the application form.
 - B. Branch should clearly state to the applicant that the cancellation of the TT cannot be made if the corresponding bank has already acted upon the initial payment instruction.
 - C. Confirmation from Nostro Bank is to be obtained whether the TT request of the bank has already been executed/debited in the bank's account maintained at nostro bank.  If the debit transaction  has  already  been  made  by  nostro,  then  the  customer's  request  cannot  be entertained and should be communicated to the customer accordingly.  For obtaining confirmation about nostro account debit, branch shall request Reconciliation Department with details of the TT transaction.  If no debit is made in the account till date, then branch shall request for Cancellation of the payment instruction .  The SWIFT message for cancellation of the payment should be forwarded promptly to SWIFT Department.
 - D. After  the  receipt  of  confirmation  of  the  cancellation  of  the  payment  instruction  from  the nostro bank, branch shall reverse the transaction and settle the amount as per request of the

<!-- image -->

customer/applicant.   Refund  of  the  amount  against  cancelled  payment  message  should  be made through credit to the customer's account.

 - E. Current  exchange  rate  or  the  rate  advised  by  treasury  department  should  be  applied  for reversal of transaction.
 - F. Branch shall recover charges for cancellation and swift message as per Standard tariff of the bank and also recover charges if any applied by the nostro bank.

## 3.2.2.4 Reconciliation of Nostro Bank Charges

Generally, outward SWIFT payment messages attract certain charges by Nostro bank in case the payment is sent with charge liability on part of the bank (charge detail as 'OUR').  Besides, nostro bank may also apply their charge in the payment in other types of charges instruction as well.

 While sending the SWIFT message, branch shall  also recover the charges upfront from the account of the applicant/customer to ensure recovery of possible charges by the nostro bank where charge is mentioned as 'OUR'.

 On monthly basis Treasury Back Office (TBO) shall review the MIS report of details of TT sent by branches and tally total charges debited by nostro as per their billings.  Province Office shall make follow-up with the branches for recovery of such charges.

## 3.2.3 Manager's Cheque

## 3.2.3.1 Issuance of Manager's Cheque upon Request of a Customer

- A. The  applicant  can  be  account  holder  of  the  bank  or  a  walk-in  customer  for  issuance  of Manager's Cheque.  The applicant should fill the standard form of the bank.   The application should be prepared in two copies and should contain
- a. Full name and address of applicant
- b. Amount in words and figures
- c. Full name and address of beneficiary and if available, the account number and contact number of the beneficiary
- d. Purpose of the Manager's Cheque
- B. Branch  shall  obtain  the  amount  along  with  the  applicable  commission  charge  from  the customer in accordance with the schedule of fees and charges of the bank.  The total amount can be received by either debiting the customer's account or in cash over the cash counter.
 - C. Branch shall make entry of the issuance of Manager's Cheque in the system and ensure that the  Manager's  Cheque  number  in  the  system  and  the  number  of  the  Manager's  Cheque printed is same.  Branch shall mention the Tran ID, Manager's Cheque number and details of amount and commission charged to the customer in the application form.
 - D. Branch shall print the Manager's Cheque from the system and check that all details printed is correct.  Handwritten Manager's Cheque should not be issued.  MC should be endorsed by cheque writer in the face of the cheque.  Manager's Cheque should be account payable and the branch should not issue bearer or general crossing (& Co.)  cheque.
 - E. Manager's Cheque should be signed by two authorized staff of the branch.  The limit for signing of demand draft should be as per the limit specified under Authorized Signatory booklet of the bank.
 - F. Branch shall record the details of Managers cheque issued in MC Issuance Register.
 - G. Branch shall obtain the signature of the applicant in the copy of the Manager's Cheque as an acknowledgement of the receipt of the MC and provide the customer copy of the application form duly signed and stamped.

## 3.2.3.2 Issuance of Manager's Cheque on Inter-Departmental Request

Manager's  Cheque  can  be  issued  on  behalf  of  other  departments  on  the  basis  of  Inter Department Memorandum/Request approved by competent authority or on email request sent by concerned Department.

 <!-- image -->

No commission should be applied for issuing the Manager's Cheque on inter departmental request.

 ## 3.2.3.3 Payment of Manager's Cheque

- A. The Manager's Cheque should not be stale.
 - B. Signature of authorized signatories on the Manager's Cheque should be verified as per the signature mentioned in the list of authorized signatories.
 - C. While making entry in the system for the payment of Manager's Cheque, the paying branch should ensure to settle correct cheque and details as recorded in the system.  Details of payee and Manager's cheque serial number must be recorded in the system.
 - D. Branch  shall  affix  'Paid'  stamp  once  the  payment  of  MC  is  made  to  the  concerned beneficiary.
 - E. On monthly basis, branch shall reconcile Managers Cheque payable account and prepare exhibit  of  unpresented  Managers  Cheque.   The  exhibit  report  of  outstanding  Managers Cheque should be forwarded to concerned Province Office for record.

 ## 3.2.3.4 Stale Manager's Cheque

Manager's Cheque issued but remaining outstanding for a period of more than six months is termed as Stale Manager's Cheque.

 ## 3.2.3.5 Cancellation and Revalidation of Manager's Cheque

- A. A Manager's Cheque may be cancelled on the receipt of an application in writing from the applicant.
 - B. Cancellation charge should be recovered as per the standard rate of the Bank.
 - C. The face of the Manager's cheque should be marked with Cancelled stamp.
 - D. The amount should be refunded to the applicant in cash or by account transfer.  In case of cash payment, photo identification documents of the applicant/customer must be obtained.
 - E. Re-issuance  of  Manager's  Cheque  in  lieu  of  cancelled  one  should  be  carried  out  as  per issuance of new Manager's Cheque.  However, issuance charge shall not be applied in case of reissuance.

metadata.window:
## 3.2.3.6 Loss of Manager's Cheque

- A. Written intimation of the loss of Manager's Cheque from the applicant/customer should be obtained.  If intimation/request is received from the payee, it should be counter signed by the applicant or a confirmation of the applicant should be obtained.
 - B. Upon receipt of the intimation/request, branch shall verify the signature of the applicant and mark timer stamp on such request.

 Branch  should  check  in  the  system  if  the  said  Manager's  cheque  is  already  paid.   If  the Manager's cheque is already paid, branch should inform the applicant immediately in writing.

 If  the  Manager's  Cheque  is  not  already  paid,  branch  shall  proceed  for  reversal  of  the Manager's cheque.  Branch shall make reverse entry of the Manager's Cheque in system and book the amount in Pool Account for settlement/refund as per applicant's/customer's request.

 Branch shall obtain applicable charge for cancellation/stop payment of the MC charge from the applicant.

 ## 3.2.3.7 Maintenance of Stock of Manager's Cheque

- A. The stock of Manager's Cheque in the branch should be kept safely in the vault/cabinet under lock.   A  Manager's  Cheque  stock  register  should  be  maintained.   The  register  should  be maintained  separately  in  the  branch  for  stock  kept  in  the  vault  and  stock  kept  in  the department for use.
 - B. Only the  necessary  quantity  of  Manager's  Cheque  should  be  handed  over  to  the  staff  of Remittance Department.

 <!-- image -->

- C. The responsibility of balancing/verification of the stock of the Manager's Cheque rests upon Operations In-charge.  And Branch Manager should check the physical stock of Manager's Cheque at least once a month to ensure no any deviation is occurred.
 - D. If any Manager's Cheque becomes invalid due to error/mistake in printing-issuance process, such cheque should be marked as Void.   Such Manager's Cheque should be noted in the Manager's Cheque issuance register with void remarks and kept in separate file for record.

- A. Written intimation of the loss of Manager's Cheque from the applicant/customer should be obtained.  If intimation/request is received from the payee, it should be counter signed by the applicant or a confirmation of the applicant should be obtained.
 - B. Upon receipt of the intimation/request, branch shall verify the signature of the applicant and mark timer stamp on such request.

 Branch  should  check  in  the  system  if  the  said  Manager's  cheque  is  already  paid.   If  the Manager's cheque is already paid, branch should inform the applicant immediately in writing.

 If  the  Manager's  Cheque  is  not  already  paid,  branch  shall  proceed  for  reversal  of  the Manager's cheque.  Branch shall make reverse entry of the Manager's Cheque in system and book the amount in Pool Account for settlement/refund as per applicant's/customer's request.

 Branch shall obtain applicable charge for cancellation/stop payment of the MC charge from the applicant.

 ## 3.2.3.7 Maintenance of Stock of Manager's Cheque

- A. The stock of Manager's Cheque in the branch should be kept safely in the vault/cabinet under lock.   A  Manager's  Cheque  stock  register  should  be  maintained.   The  register  should  be maintained  separately  in  the  branch  for  stock  kept  in  the  vault  and  stock  kept  in  the department for use.
 - B. Only the  necessary  quantity  of  Manager's  Cheque  should  be  handed  over  to  the  staff  of Remittance Department.

 <!-- image -->

- C. The responsibility of balancing/verification of the stock of the Manager's Cheque rests upon Operations In-charge.  And Branch Manager should check the physical stock of Manager's Cheque at least once a month to ensure no any deviation is occurred.
 - D. If any Manager's Cheque becomes invalid due to error/mistake in printing-issuance process, such cheque should be marked as Void.   Such Manager's Cheque should be noted in the Manager's Cheque issuance register with void remarks and kept in separate file for record.

## 3.3 Advance Payment Certificate (APC)

APC is the confirmation letter issued by the bank upon receipt of advance payment on account of a customer.  APC is used as an export instrument for making export of goods/ services by Nepalese exporters.  It is to be issued at the request of the customer as per the provisions outlined in NRB's Unified Foreign Exchange Circulars-2080, Circular no.  5/2080.

 The bank has already developed digital platform for generation system printed APC as per the format prescribed by NRB and branches must use the same platform for printing APC.

 ## 3.4 Checks and Review

- A. Branch shall carry out reconciliation of Manager's Cheque payable account on monthly basis  and  prepare  exhibit  of  unpresented  Manager's  cheque  and  forward  to  concerned Province Office.
 - B. Operation In-charge shall on daily basis check and reconcile the stock of security printings and stationery like bank draft, manager's cheque, Bi.Bi.Ni forms, etc.  Branch Manager shall on monthly basis check and verify the stock of security printings and stationery.
 - C. Operation In-charge shall on daily basis check for necessary reporting of Draft/TT issuance, follow-up  for  Bi.Bi.Ni  forms,  settlement  of  margin  held  and  NRB  cheque  issued  for Draft/TT issuance transactions.
 - D. Operation In-charge shall on daily basis ensure that detailed list of demand draft issued by the branch is forwarded to Branch Operations to send draft confirmation message to the nostro banks.
 - E. Branch Operations shall be responsible for sending Bank Draft confirmation message to the nostro banks on daily basis.
 - F. This manual shall supersede the existing Outward Remittance Manual and other circulars issued which have been incorporated herein.
 - G. In  case  of  any  new  provisions  or  guidelines  is  introduced  through  directives,  circulars issued by NRB and/or any regulatory authority, the same shall prevail.
 - H. Exception: Any exception to the provisions made in this manual is subject to the approval as defined in Operational Approving Authority Matrix.

## CHAPTER 4 SAFE DEPOSIT LOCKER (VAULT) - OPERATIONS MANUAL

## 4.1 Locker Operations

For the safety of valuables, the locker facility offers a safe, trustworthy space to store them.  Bank provides customers with individual safe deposit locker for the safekeeping of their valuable items.  Renting of a locker establishes a contractual relationship between the bank and the customer.

 Locker is normally offered in the various sizes.  Lockers shall be located in a strong room and generally separated from other sections of the bank with additional security arrangement for safeguarding of customers' valuable items kept in the locker.  Following are the basic features related to locker service:

-  Each locker shall be equipped with a dual control lock operated by the use of the common key held by the Bank and the customer's key held by the customer.
 -  The locker entrance must be covered under CCTV recording.
 -  Employee of the bank shall not have custody of customer's locker or have in his/her possession a customer's key.
 -  Allotment of lockers is on first-come-first-served basis.  At the time of hiring the  locker,  bank  will  obtain  a  minimum-security  deposit  from  the  locker holder (also referred hereafter as lessee) which will be decided by the bank from time to time.
 -  Lessee  of  a  safe  deposit  locker  (vault)  can  appoint  another  person  for operating the locker, on the terms and conditions in rent agreement and the authority in favor of the said person ceases with the death of the lessee.
 -  The locker holders shall not be permitted to use the locker for the deposit of weapons  or  any  liquid  or  anything  of  explosive,  dangerous  or  offensive nature or any other illegal objects.

For the safety of valuables, the locker facility offers a safe, trustworthy space to store them.  Bank provides customers with individual safe deposit locker for the safekeeping of their valuable items.  Renting of a locker establishes a contractual relationship between the bank and the customer.

 Locker is normally offered in the various sizes.  Lockers shall be located in a strong room and generally separated from other sections of the bank with additional security arrangement for safeguarding of customers' valuable items kept in the locker.

## CHAPTER 4 SAFE DEPOSIT LOCKER (VAULT) - OPERATIONS MANUAL

## 4.1 Locker Operations

For the safety of valuables, the locker facility offers a safe, trustworthy space to store them.  Bank provides customers with individual safe deposit locker for the safekeeping of their valuable items.  Renting of a locker establishes a contractual relationship between the bank and the customer.

 Locker is normally offered in the various sizes.  Lockers shall be located in a strong room and generally separated from other sections of the bank with additional security arrangement for safeguarding of customers' valuable items kept in the locker.  Following are the basic features related to locker service:

-  Each locker shall be equipped with a dual control lock operated by the use of the common key held by the Bank and the customer's key held by the customer.
 -  The locker entrance must be covered under CCTV recording.
 -  Employee of the bank shall not have custody of customer's locker or have in his/her possession a customer's key.
 -  Allotment of lockers is on first-come-first-served basis.  At the time of hiring the  locker,  bank  will  obtain  a  minimum-security  deposit  from  the  locker holder (also referred hereafter as lessee) which will be decided by the bank from time to time.
 -  Lessee  of  a  safe  deposit  locker  (vault)  can  appoint  another  person  for operating the locker, on the terms and conditions in rent agreement and the authority in favor of the said person ceases with the death of the lessee.
 -  The locker holders shall not be permitted to use the locker for the deposit of weapons  or  any  liquid  or  anything  of  explosive,  dangerous  or  offensive nature or any other illegal objects.

## 4.2 Eligibility

- A. The Bank's Safe Deposit Locker (Vault) Service is made available to those customers (person and entity) who maintain a Savings/Current Account (individually or jointly).
 - B. Minor, mentally disabled and blacklisted persons shall not be eligible to avail the facility.  Lockers can be leased out to physically disabled (differently abled), blind person as well.  Physically  disabled  (differently  abled)  person  shall  be  provided  privilege  service  in choosing and availing locker service as per the ease of the customer.
 - C. In case of lockers to be leased out to blind and illiterate person, they shall be allowed to appoint any mandatee and/or nominee in operation of the locker service in presence of bank official.  KYC documents of mandatee and/or nominee also to be obtained.  Mandatee for blind/illiterate is applicable for the locker facility only.
 - D. In case of individual customer, the locker holder can authorize any other person (mandatee) to  operate the locker.  KYC form along with identification documents of the authorized person (mandatee) must be obtained.  Mandatee shall not be eligible to appoint any other mandatee.
 - E. In case of locker in joint name, mode of operations must be clearly obtained.  In case of locker opened jointly, each locker operator can operate the locker either individually or jointly as per instruction provided in the Locker Application Form.
 - F. In case of corporate entity, the locker should be in the name of the firm/company/institution.  The  firm/company/institution  should  submit  a  written  request/resolution/authorization

<!-- image -->

letter to the bank for renting out of the locker and authorizing any person(s) to operate the locker on behalf of the firm/company/institution.  The name and specimen signature of the locker operator(s) must be disclosed in the request letter/ board resolution/authorization letter.   KYC  form  along  with  identification  documents  of  the  authorized  person/locker operator must be obtained.

metadata.title: Unified Branch Operations Manual
metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 4.3 Procedure for Issuance of Locker

- A. Branch  shall  obtain  duly  filled  Locker  Application  Form  as  per  standard  format.   The signature of the customer must be verified with the specimen signature maintained with the bank.   Mode  of  operation  of  the  locker  (single,  joint,  mandate,  etc.)   must  be  clearly mentioned in the Locker Application Form and Signature Specimen Card.  All these details should be updated in Finacle (CBS).
 - B. Branch  shall  obtain  three  copies  of  recent  passport  size  photograph  of  the  locker operator(s).   One  photo  should  be  affixed  in  the  application  form,  one  in  Locker  Visit Register and another in the Customer Identity Card for locker.
 - C. Declaration/indemnity from the customer regarding the goods prohibited as per NRB guidelines to be taken.
 - D. In  case  the locker is  to  be  operated  by  a  mandatee, Locker Authorization Letter as per standard format should be obtained along with two recent passport size photograph and identification documents of the mandatee.
 - E. In case of appointment of nominee, branch shall obtain Nominee(s), Form filled-up and signed by the applicant along with identification documents of the nominee.
 - F. Allotment of lockers shall be on first-come-first-served basis.  The bank has the right to deny providing locker facility without providing any reason(s) to the customer if any locker is not available vacant in the branch.  The customer may be allowed to choose the locker on availability of vacant lockers in the branch.
 - G. The customer's request for locker service should be approved by Operations In-charge or Branch Manager.  Branch shall issue the locker to the  customer  upon  receipt  of  all  the documents  and  recovering  necessary  locker  deposit  and  annual  locker  rental  charge  in advance.
 - H. Risk grading and CDD review procedures of the locker holders should be carried out by the branch.
 - In case of locker to be provided to the high-risk customer, account of such customer to be approved as by the concerned authority as per AML/CFT guidelines as per existing rules and approval assignment of Locker to be done by Branch Manager of the concerned branch.
 - I. The key deposit shall be auto hold/lien marked and the locker rental shall be auto debited by the system in the account of the customer in advance.
 - J. Upon approval, branch shall assign the locker to the customer and note/mark the locker number and key number in the application form.

metadata.window:
## 4.4 Locker Key Deposit

- A. The locker key deposit should be obtained at the time of providing a locker to the customer.  The locker key deposit must be earmarked in the account of the customer till the termination of the locker agreement or cancellation of the locker service by the customer.  This shall be auto arranged in the locker module.
 - B. For the account where the minimum balance of the deposit product is more than the locker key deposit, branch must also mark lien for key deposit amount.
 - C. In case the customer requests to discontinue the locker service, the earmarked amount of locker key deposit will be auto released and branch shall obtain the locker key back from the  customer  after  ensuring  that  the  locker  is  empty  upon  receiving  locker  closure application form.
 - D. Branch shall not allow the customer to withdraw fund in the account by releasing the lien under any circumstances unless the locker is surrendered by the customer.
 - E. In case the customer avails bigger size locker than the existing size, branch shall recover the additional key deposit for the bigger sized locker.
 - F. The  locker  key  deposit,  locker  surrender  charge,  locker  change(Branch/Size)  shall  be waived for GIBL staff until the tenure in bank service.

- A. The locker key deposit should be obtained at the time of providing a locker to the customer.  The locker key deposit must be earmarked in the account of the customer till the termination of the locker agreement or cancellation of the locker service by the customer.  This shall be auto arranged in the locker module.
 - B. For the account where the minimum balance of the deposit product is more than the locker key deposit, branch must also mark lien for key deposit amount.
 - C. In case the customer requests to discontinue the locker service, the earmarked amount of locker key deposit will be auto released and branch shall obtain the locker key back from the  customer  after  ensuring  that  the  locker  is  empty  upon  receiving  locker  closure application form.
 - D. Branch shall not allow the customer to withdraw fund in the account by releasing the lien under any circumstances unless the locker is surrendered by the customer.
 - E. In case the customer avails bigger size locker than the existing size, branch shall recover the additional key deposit for the bigger sized locker.
 - F. The  locker  key  deposit,  locker  surrender  charge,  locker  change(Branch/Size)  shall  be waived for GIBL staff until the tenure in bank service.

## 4.5 Locker Rent

- A. The locker rent shall be obtained automatically in advance as per the standard tariff of fees and charges of the bank.  The locker rent is non-refundable either partially or in full even if the locker service is discontinued or cancelled by the customer during the tenure of the locker agreement.
 - B. Tenure  of  locker  rental  shall  be  for  one  year.   Customer's  account  shall  be  debited automatically to recover the locker rental fee on due date for another tenure.
 - C. In case there is insufficient balance on due date in the account of the customer, branch shall make follow up with the customer to make necessary deposit in the account and upon deposit  of  necessary  amount,  the  applicable  rental  charge  shall  be  auto  debited  by  the system.

 <!-- image -->

- D. In case of requirement or if demanded by the customer, the branch may provide a debit advice for the locker rental charge recovered.
 - E. In case the customer avails bigger size locker than the existing size, branch shall recover the rental fee as new issuance of the locker.  In such case, remaining rental may be included while recovering rental for bigger size locker.
 - F. Branch shall suspend the locker service in case the customer fails to provide locker rental fee.   In  case  of  suspension  of  the  locker  service,  a  note  having  such  suspension  remark should be attached in the Locker Operation form of the customer.
 - G. In case of GIBL staff, 50% discount shall be provided on the standard tariff of the bank in locker rental.  However, once the staff leaves from the bank services, such waiver shall not be provided.

metadata.window:
## 4.6 Procedure to Operate Locker

- A. Management and handling of key to Locker Room, Common Key of Locker and key to unrented Locker shall be as follows:
- a) Key to the strong room of Locker: to be kept in vault with joint custody of Vault Key Holders
- b) Common  Key  of Locker: to be kept by Operation In-charge/CSD Incharge/designated staff          in the vault/ fire proof cabinet
- c) Key  of  unrented  Locker:  to  be  kept  in  vault  with  joint  custody  of  Vault  Key Holders.  Common Key Holders must not be in the possession of unrented locker keys at any point of time.

 Handover of key of locker room and Common Key of the Locker between Operation Incharge, CSD In-charge or Locker attending staff must be recorded in the Key Register.

 All  spare  keys  of  Locker  Strong  Room  and  Locker  are  to  be  kept  in  Locker  of another nearby branches/banks or vault of other branches with due approval from concerned authority as per Approving Authority Matrix.

 - B.  The service shall be provided during regular office hour.  The staff at Customer Service Department or the locker attendant facilitates customers on visit to the locker.

 Any unauthorized person shall be restricted to visit the Locker room.

 - C. On visit to the locker, by locker holder, branch shall follow the procedures as mentioned below:
- a) The staff at CSD shall request the customer for presentment of Locker Identity Card and verify the  signature,  photograph  of  locker  holder/operator  and  locker details along with the Locker Visit Register/locker specimen card held with the bank.
 - b) The  staff  shall  check  the  customer  details  like  locker  holder/operator's  name, locker number and Customer Identity Card for Locker and any special instruction for locker operation recorded in the form/locker specimen card.
 - c) Branch shall record the detail of the customer in the Locker Visit Register as per standard format and verify the signature of the customer.  The details must include:
-  Date of visit
-  Time in of locker visit
-  Signature of the customer
-  Signature of staff in the department

 <!-- image -->

- d) Branch shall ensure that customers of two different lockers are not allowed to visit the locker room or open the locker at the same time.  Once the customer comes out from locker room, concerned staff to ensure that any belongings are left or locker is locked or not and then only another customer shall be allowed to enter into the locker room.
 - e) The staff at CSD shall open the locker in front of the customer.  The staff shall first insert the Common Key of the bank and request the customer to insert his/her key to open the locker.
 - f) Once the customer opens the locker by applying his/her keys, the staff shall remove the Common Key of the bank and keep the key with self and give complete privacy to the locker holder/operator.  The staff, at any circumstances, shall not assist the locker holder to handle the contents/items for keeping in/out of the locker.  The customer should not be allowed to leave the locker room un-noticed by the staff attending for locker service.
 - g) The staff must ensure that safe deposit locker opened by the customer is properly closed  before  the  customer  has  left  the  locker  room.   The  staff  must  record  the 'Time of exit' of customer in the Locker Visit Register once the customer left the locker room.  This shall also be registered in the new locker module.  The staff must check and examine the locker room properly at the time of exit of the customer to ensure that no any contents/items or customer belongings or any key is left out in the Locker Room.
 - h) In case where the staff finds the locker key or any contents of the locker, the staff must  immediately  report  to  the  Operations  In-charge/Branch  Manager.   Branch shall note the time and make a list of such contents/item to be kept in vault.
 - i) The contents/items may be provided back to the customer on detailed investigation with due approval.  The minimum approving authority shall be Dy HOP/HOP.  The customer  needs  to      acknowledge  the  receipt  of  the  items  handed  back  by  the branch.  The receipt of acknowledgement must be kept in the file of the customer for record purpose.

 - i) The contents/items may be provided back to the customer on detailed investigation with due approval.  The minimum approving authority shall be Dy HOP/HOP. metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 4.7 Event of Default

- A. On daily basis, branch shall review the locker rental payment details to ascertain whether locker rental fee is due for any locker in the branch.  If the locker rental fee could not be recovered due to insufficient balance in the customer's account, branch shall inform the customer to make necessary deposit in the account.
 - B. The locker should  be  suspended  in  case  of  non-recovery  of  locker  rental  on  due  date.  Suspended option is available in new locker module.
 - C. In case the customer fails to make deposit in the account for locker rental fee within 3 months of due date, the customer should be communicated in writing for payment of due

<!-- image -->

rental fee.  A reminder letter should be communicated if the customer fails to pay the due locker rental fee within 1 month of the first notice.  Late fee charge will be application in such case.

 - D. If  the  customer  fails  to  response  positively  or  pay  due  rental  fee  despite  the  bank's notification, a 35 days' notice should be published in a national daily newspaper at the cost of the customer upon approval from Province Office.
 - E. If the customer still fails to clear his/her locker rental due, branch shall proceed for recovery action of all rental and due amount.  Branch shall obtain approval from Dy HOP/HOP for breaking open the locker and if required, legal opinion from Legal Department shall be obtained before breaking open the locker.

metadata.window:
The locker shall be broken in presence of the following officials' representatives:

- a) Operations In-charge
- b) Branch Manager
- c) Representative of locker supplier company
- d) Representative from local police authority
- e) Representative of ward office or local government authority
- F. A list of contents/items recovered from the broken locker must be prepared and attested with the signature of officials/representatives present during locker  break-open process.  The contents of the locker must be kept in possession of the branch.
 - G. The contents/items recovered should be disposed off as per the decision of management and approval from as per Operational Approving Authority Matrix  to recover all rental dues,  fixing  charge  and  other  dues  in  relation  to  the  locker  of  the  customer  and residual/remaining amount to be deposited in the account of the customer.
 - H. Branch shall fix up the broken locker in coordination with General Service department and such locker shall be treated as unoccupied locker available for new issuance.
 - I. The representative  other  than  bank  staff/official  shall  be  provided  specified  allowance; required tax to be deducted and receipt to be prepared and kept in the record.  Such expenses are to be settled/recovered as receivable from the concerned locker holder.

metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 4.8 Loss of Key

- A. In case of loss of the key, branch shall obtain a written request from the customer with regard to the loss of key of the locker.
 - B. On receipt of the request letter, branch shall suspend the locker in system and the locker must be broken.  The key must be changed/replaced at the cost of the customer.
 - C. In case of information/instruction received over the phone from the customer for the loss of locker key, branch shall immediately suspend the operation of the locker.  The date and time of information/instruction received over the phone must be recorded in the Locker Application Form and Locker Visit Register.  Branch shall follow up with the customer to obtain a written request.
 - D. On verification of the customer's request and signature, branch shall forward the request to break the locker upon approval to province office.
 - E. The locker should be broken in the  presence  of  the customer,  Operations  In-charge  or Branch Manager, staff from Customer Service department handling locker service and the representative from the vendor should be present at the time of locker break-open.
 - F. After breaking open the locker, the customer should be allowed to take possession of the contents/items kept by the customer in the locker.  A declaration regarding

<!-- image -->

acknowledgement  of  all  the  contents/items  in  the  locker  should  be  obtained  from  the customer.

 - G. Actual expenses related to breaking-open the locker, repairing and fixing the same and replacing the fresh key (as per standard tariff of the bank) should be recovered from the customer.
 - H. The customer can be assigned a new locker as per request if available in the branch.  Branch shall follow the standard procedures as mentioned above in case of issuance of new locker to the customer.

## 4.9 Death of Locker Holder

- A. The general procedures for settlement of claim over the locker of deceased person are same as  in  case  of  claim  on  bank  account  of  deceased  customer.   The  locker  should  be immediately suspended upon receipt of information/notice of death of the locker holder.  The contents thereof kept in the locker should be provided to the nominated person(s) or the legal heir(s) of the locker holder.
 - B. Branch shall follow procedures as follows:
- a) Upon receipt of information/notice of the death of the locker holder, branch shall suspend operation of the locker in system and Locker Visit Register.  The Locker Application Form should be kept in separate file with a note of restriction in locker operation.
 - b) A written request from the nominee or legal heir should be obtained for the claim over the contents of the locker along with following documents:
-  Identification document copy of the applicant
-  Death Registration Certificate
-  Relationship Certificate
-  Locker Identity Card of the Locker Holder
- c) Branch shall forward the request of the Applicant along with all other documents of  locker  operation  to  concerned  Province  Office.   The  minimum  approving authority shall be as per Operational Approving Authority Matrix.
 - d) The  contents/items  kept  in  the  locker  shall  be  provided  to  the  Applicant  upon verification of the documents and satisfaction of the request of the Applicant and recommendation by the branch.  In case of locker where the nominee is assigned, branch shall provide the contents/items to the nominee, otherwise a 35 days' notice shall be published in a national daily newspaper.
 - e) Where any doubt is raised on the request of the Applicant, a public notice at the cost of the customer should be published in a national daily newspaper with details of person deceased, name of the claimant/nominee, and relationship of Applicant with deceased person.  Such cost to be borne by the applicant.
 - f) If any claim during the period is not received, the Applicant shall be allowed to receive the contents of the locker and a letter of acknowledgement regarding receipt of all the contents of the locker by the Applicant shall be obtained.
 - g) If  any  claim  is  received  or  dispute  is  raised,  branch  shall  consult  with  Legal department for  further  settlement  of  the  claim  and/or  dispute  through  Province Office.

metadata.author: Bikash Thapa
metadata.window:
## 4.10 Discontinuation of Locker

- A. The locker service provided to the customer is automatically renewed for tenure of next one year, until and unless the customer requests the bank for discontinuation of the service.  Branch shall on its own recover annual locker rental fee in advance from the customer.  In case the locker holder/customer wants to discontinue the locker service, the customer needs to submit a written request before the expiry of the rental period.
 - B. Branch shall obtain a written application along with Locker Identity Card and the locker key from the locker holder.
 - C. The signature of the customer in the request letter must be verified and the request should be forwarded to Operations In-charge or Branch Manager for approval.  If the locker rental fee is due and remains un-recovered, the same should be recovered first from the locker holder prior to closure of the locker service.
 - D. Upon approval, locker holder should be allowed to visit the locker room for vacating the Locker.  The staff from Customer Service department, in presence of the customer, should ensure that the locker has been completely vacated by the locker holder/customer before receiving the Locker key back from the customer.  The staff at Customer Service department shall take possession of the key.
 - E. A  declaration  from  the  customer  regarding  withdrawal  of  all  the  contents/items  of  the locker should be obtained at the time of locker closure.
 - F. The surrendered locker key should be kept in a sealed envelope signed by Operations Incharge or Branch Manager and concerned staff of Customer Service department and should be kept in Vault/Locker till next issuance.  The locker shall be treated as available locker for issuance to a new customer.  The locker shall be rented out to another customer as per above mentioned procedures.
 - G. Mandatee shall not to be allowed to request for discontinuation of locker.

## 4.11 Locker Access Blocked

- A. There  are  certain  instances  where  instruction  for  block/restriction/suspension  on  locker operation is received from Nepal Rastra Bank and/or other regulatory government authority or court.
 - B. Upon  receipt  of  such  instruction,  branch  shall  immediately  block/restrict/suspend  the operation of the locker.  The Compliance department/Corporate Office of the Bank shall also provide instruction in relation to block/restriction of locker.
 - C. Branch shall follow procedures as follows:

<!-- image -->

- i. The  document  of  locker  of  the  customer  should  be  kept  in  a separate file in the vault
- ii.  Branch shall mark a notation of 'Locker Block/Restriction/Suspension for Operation' in the Locker Application  Form  and  Locker  Visit  Register  and  immediately suspend the said locker in new locker module.
 - iii.  In no circumstance, the locker holder/customer should be allowed to visit/operate the locker.

- A. In  case  of  locker  to  be  relocated  from  one  branch  to  another,  branch  shall  proceed  as follows:
- i. Branch shall arrange to invite the representatives from Local Government Bodies, Area Police Office as well as concerned customers on date and time as approved by the Management.
 - ii.  Branch  shall  send  the  invitation  letters  to  representatives  from  local government bodies and Area Police Office for relocating the safe deposit lockers in prescribed format.
 - iii.  Locker to be relocated in presence of following:
- a) Operations In-charge
- b) Branch Manager
- c) Representative of locker supplier company (if available)
- d) Representative from area police office
- e) Representative of local government bodies
- f) Concerned customers (if available)
- B. A 'muchulka' as per prescribed format should be raised upon relocation of lockers and attested with the signature of officials/representatives/concerned customers present during relocation process.

 <!-- image -->

- C. Branch  shall  arrange  to  publish  a  public  notice  regarding  relocation  of  locker  in coordination with Province Office and Marketing Departments upon relocating the lockers for customer's information.

 ## 4.13 Checks and Review

- A. This manual shall supersede previous manual in relation to the safe deposit locker (vault) operations of the bank.
 - B. The  manual  shall  be  reviewed  every  year  or  as  deemed  necessary  and  any  updates  or amendments if required shall be incorporated accordingly.  In case of any new provisions or  guidelines  is  introduced  through  directives,  circulars  issued  by  NRB  and/or  any regulatory authority, the same shall prevail.
 - C. Any provisions under this manual which are not clear/ambiguous shall be interpreted by CEO.  The authority of waiver of any provisions shall rest upon CEO.

metadata.window:
## 3, Intcrnal  Audit Function

- 3.1 Bank shall establish  a permanent and independent intemal audit department within its organizational  stnrcture.
 - 3.2 Intemal  Audit  Charter framed in Section  C of this document shall  guide the intemal  audit function in bank which includes the purpose,  visiorq  mission,  values, structure, scope of work, authority  and responsibility,  professional standards and code ofethics,  etc.  ofthe Intemal  Audit Department.
 - 3.3 Intemal  audit department shall frame necessary operational procedures  and guidelines required to streamline  the intemal  audit functions with the scope  of intemal audit charter.
 - 3.4 The intemal audit function  of bank shall be held accountable to the audit committee,  on all matters  related  to the  performance of its mandate  as described in the intemal  audit charter.
 - 3.5 Internal  audit department shall submil  at least,  quarterly  reports to the audit committee  of its affairs  and important  findings.
 - 3.6 The head of intemal  audit department shall be responsible  for ensuring  that the department complies with sound intemal  auditing  standards and a relevant code ofethics.
 - 3.7 Intemal  audit activities  shall be conducted  by the bank's own intemal  audit stafl however, bank may outsource  the extemal resources for intemal audit specific  purpose  as deemed necessary  by committee or board.
 - 3.8 Intemal auditors shall have no line responsibility or authority over any of the operations they examine.  The intemal audit shall independently  assess  the effectiveness  and efficiency  of the intemal  control, risk management,  compliance,  govemance systems  and processes and ensure that they are  functioning within given framework.
 - 3.9 Board and management shall ensure that adequate/required  skilled resources are placed  in intemal audit department  considering nature, size and complexity of its works and scope to carry out its duties independently.
 - 3.10 The intemal audit function, whenever relevant to the performance  of its assignments  will have full and unconditional  access to any records,  files, data and physical properties ofthe bank.  This includes management information  systems, records and the minutes of all consultative  and decision-making  bodies.
 - 3.11 Internal audit function  shall cover  all the business  and control  functions in bank for audit as directed  by audit committee,  board and regulators  from  time to time in conjunction  with the risk profile  ofbank and those auditable units.

## .1.   External/StatutorvAuditFunction

- 4.1 The Bank shall conduct an annual extemal audit of its financial  statements by independent chartered  accountants,  individually or jointly  within  prescribed  time frame in line with the provision of prevailing  Bank  and Financial  Institutions Ac!  Company  Act and relevant NRB Directives.
 - 4.2 Any additional responsibilities  to the extemal auditors will be determined  annually in conjunction  with the Bank's  risk review,  as determined by the audit committee  and board.
 - 4.3 The appointment,  dismissal,  remuneration,  scope,  power  and duties, etc.  of extemal/statutory auditor shall be in compliance with the provisions  of relevant Acts and Regulations.

 ## 5.  Special Purpose  Audit Function

- 5.1 Special  audit assignments  shall be conducted  in bank focusing  on prime  risk areas as identified from regular audit functions,  as advised  by management,  audit committee,  board  and as part of regulatory/supervisory  requirement.
 - 5.2 Internally or extemally,  the lnformation  System, Management, Cost Audit,  Revenue,  Propriety, Risk Management,  Non-Performing Assets, Anti Money Laundering,  Loan Write-off,  adequacy and effectiveness of intemal policies  and procedures,  and such other special audits alike them shall be conducted  by bank  fiom time to time on need  basis within the scope ofthis policy.

 ## 6.  Investigation  Function

Investigation  shall  be carried out in particular  cases as identified/directed  by the board, audit committee and management.

 - 6.1 Investigations are critically  reviewed using different approaches  as deemed suitable by the department.
 - 6.2 Normally, intemal  investigation  on affairs ofbank  shall be done by the intemal audit department in coordination  with other  relevant  departments  and persons.  However,  Bank can use third party investigation  experts if such resources are not available  and use of such third  parties is considered  necessary by the department  and committee.
 - 6.3 Scope, authority and resources  required for investigations  to be provided  by bank to conclude investigations  in time.

However,  Bank can use third party investigation  experts if such resources are not available  and use of such third  parties is considered  necessary by the department  and committee.

## 13.   Quality  Control  and Supcrvision  of Audit Activities

- 13.1 Internal Auditors  shall comply  with  the provision  ofNepal  Standard on  Quality  Control(NSQCI )  issued  by Auditing Standard Board.
 - 13.2 The audit committee  shall regularly  monitor and supervise  the quality and effectiveness ofthe work performed  by the intemal  auditor, extemal auditor, and other specialized auditor(s).
 - 13.3  Quality  control  and supervision  responsibility  of all internal audit assignments,  whether performed by/or for the intemal  audit, remain  with the head of intemal  audit department.
 - 13.4 The head of intemal  audit  department shall conduct  quality assurance  reviews on the work performed  by the intemal audit staffs and ensure that issues identified  are followed up in time and corrective  actions are taken,  where  necessary.

 ## l.l.  ltcporting and Conrmunication  of Audit Function

- 14.1 After completion  ofaudit assignments  by the intemal  auditors, audit reports  shall be forwarded to the audit committee  and board.  At the same  time, a copy ofthe report shall be forwarded to

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- management  for necessary corrective action along  with suggestions,  instructions,  and directions as the case may be.
 - 14.2 The extemal auditor shall communicate  audit matters of govemance  interest arising  from the audit offinancial  statements with audit  committee and board  as per relevant  Nepal  Standards on Auditing  (NSA).
 - 14.3 Internal  Audit Department is required to report  to audit committee  clearly indicating  the progress/achievement  against  approved  audit plan, summary of major findings  and specific recommendations, changes, ifany in approved  audit plan,  etc.  for review.
 - 14.4 The audit committee  shall report to the board of directors  about committee's activities, audit activities,  audit issues/findings,  and related  recommendations on regularity, economy, rationale and effectiveness ofthe operations  and processes  including risk management  ofthe bank.
 - 14.5 Communication  between  the audit committee and management  and staffs shall be done through the member  secretary  of audit committee.

## 15.  Enforcement  of Audit Findings

- 15.1 The intemal audit department shall be responsible for follow-up on the enforcement  status of findings and recommendations of supervisory inspections, statutory  audit remark  and intemal audit remarks.
 - 15.2 Bank shall have a strong  enforcement mechanism to ensure  compliance  with the findings of supervisory inspection,  intemal  audil  extemal audit and other special  audits.
 - 15.3 Management  shall ensure corrective action plan and review mechanism  on the findings  of auditors and supervisors  to ensure full compliance,  closure  and execution  ofrecommendations.  Intemal audit department shall monitor  the execution and correction  status as identified  in the audit reports  and update the progress  to the audit committee  on quarterly  basis.

 ## 16.  Profcssional  Standards and Code of Ethics for Auditors

- 16.1 The Audito(s)  and all audit member(s)  are required  to ensure  adherence to the highest  standards of professionalism  and ethics promulgated  by the Institute of Chartered Accountants  of Nepal (ICAN).   This shall in no way dilute the obligation  of every staff member  to adhere  to the Employee's Bylaw or any other Regulations  as applicable to all other  staffmembers  ofthe Bank by virtue oftheir  employment  in the Bank.
 - 16.2 The activities  of the principal auditor  and its staff  members,  shall be canied out in accordance with the Code ofEthics for Professional  Accountants in the Business/Practice ofthe Institute  of Chartered  Accountants of Nepal.

It shall be the responsibility of Risk Management Committee to coordinate with the audit committee to develop  sound  culture  ofrisk  management  and implement  risk based  audit approach  in bank.

 ## 21.  Responsibilities  of Scnior Management for Audit Function

- 2l.l Management shall be responsible for developing an intemal control framework  that identifies, measures, monitors  and controls all risls faced by the bank.
 - 21.2 Maintaining  an organizational  structure that clearly  assigns responsibility, authority and reporting  relationships  and ensures  that delegated  responsibilities  are effectively  carried out.

## Section  -B  Audit Committee Charter

## L  An Introduction

The Audit Committee  is the committee  of the Board  of Directors formed  pursuant to Section 60 of Bank and Financial  Institution Act 2073 and section  164 ofthe Companies Act 2063.  Its function  is to assist the Board of Directors in carrying out its responsibilities  as they relate to matters such as; financial reporting  and audits,  including  intemal  controls,  compliance  and risk management,  in line with provisions  of Unified Directive 6 ofNepal Rastra Bank (NRB).   Provisions  outlined  in the Acts state  that  there shall  be an Audit Committee  Charter, containing  the Committee's  terms of reference as approved by the Board to govem  the operations of the Commiftee and accordingly this Audit Committee Charter has been framed and implemented in bank.

 Audit committee/board  shall review this charter annually or as deemed appropriate.  Amendment/revision to this charter  shall be approved  by the board on recommendation  of audit committee.   The amendment/ revision shall be effective only after the approval  of the Board. ## 6.   Mcetings and Procecdings

- 6.1.  The committee shall hold its meetings,  at least, four times a year  and at such other  times of the year as may be required/determined  by the committee and/or  required by the Board.
 - 6.2.  Reasonable  notice of meetings  and the business  to be conducte4  together  with all relevant supporting documentation,  shall  be distributed at least two days prior to a meeting to the members  of the committee and through any electronic means or post.
 - 6.3.  The meeting  may take place physically  or digitally at the head  office  or any other place as appropriate.
 - 6.4.  Committee member or invitee may raise  issues or make  proposals  for consideration at committee meetings,  provided  the matters  raised are supported  by a committee  member.
 - 6.5.  The secretary shall take minutes  of meetings, which  shall be reviewed and approved by the members ofthe committee and signed by the committee members at the next scheduled meeting.
 - 6.6.  The minutes ofall committee meetings  shall record the proceedings,  approval taken and reasons thereof and the recommendations  to be made  to the board.  The minutes/reports  shall be submitted to the Board.
 - 6.7.  Coordinator of audit committee shall apprise  the board on committee's findings and recommendations.
 - 6.8.  The member  of audit committee shall opt to abstain  from the meeting in case of agenda  having any conflicts of interest.

## 8.4 Responsibility Regarding External Audit Function

- 8.4.1.  Overseeing  the statutory audit ofthe amual and consolidated accouns;
- 8.4.2.  Formulate guidelines required  to be observed for selection  and appointment  of auditors.  Recommend possible extemal auditors and determine  their remuneration  and other benefits, and other engagement  terms.
 - Review the extemal  auditors' proposed  audit scope  and approaclq including coordination  of audit effort with intemal  audit.  8.4.3.
 - Review the performance and code ofconduct ofthe extemal auditors.  8,4.4.
 - Review and confirm the independence  ofthe extemal auditors by obtaining  statements from the auditors  on relationships between the auditors  and the Banlq including  non-audit services, and discussing  the relationships with the auditors.  8.4.5.
 - On a regular basis, meet with the extemal auditors  to discuss on key matters  arising fiom the statutory audit  or extemal audit, and in particular any identified material weaknesses  in intemal  control in relation to the financial  reporting  process.  8.4.6.
 - Make sure that all details and information such as Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) set by regulatory  body form part  ofthe audit report.  8.4.7.
 - Discuss  the written representations  which  statutory auditor  request  from senior  management including  those  related  to govemance; 8.4.8.

 - 8.5.2.  Review the findings ofany examinations by regulatory  agencies.
 - 8.5.3.  Obtain regular updates from management  regarding compliance  matters.

## Section  -C  Internal  Audit Charter

## l. An lntroduction

Bank shall view intemal  auditing  as an independent, objective  assurance  and consulting activity designed to add value  and improve  bank's operations  and risk management  system.   Effective intemal audit provides independent  assurance  to the board  of directors and senior  management  on the quality and effectiveness  ofa bank's intemal control, risk management  and govemance  systems and processes by bringing  a systematic,  disciplined  approach to evaluate  and improve  the effectiveness  of risk management,  control and governance processes  in bank.  In addition to this, intemal audit function shall assist  the management and board in achieving  the objectives of the bank by evaluating  the effectiveness of controls and developing  recommendations for the enhancement  or improvement  of the processes  through  which accountability  is ensured, the bank's  values are preserved  and potential risks are identified and mitigated.

 This charter articulates the purpose,  standing and authority ofthe intemal audit function  within  the bank in a manner lhat  promotes  an effective intemal audit function.  To establish and operate  such robust intemal  audit function with appropriate authority, resources, structure  and operational mechanism,  this charter  has been framed  and implemented which shall provide  prudent guidelines for effective  intemal audit environment  in bank.   Audit  Policy of bank briefly summarizes  the policies  of bank related  to intemal  audit function,  this Intemal Audit Charter aligns to the same and gives substance  to those  policies.   Therefore, in line with  the Audit Policy  ofBank,  this Intemal  Audit Charter has been ftamed including  the purpose, vision,  mission, values,  structure,  scope  ofwork, authority  and responsibility,  professional  standards  and code of ethics, and other operating  guidelines  essential  for the function  of the intemal audit department.  This intemal audit charter also facilitates the understanding  and acceptance ofthe provisions  related to intemal  audit function by the managemen!  audit commirtee and board  ofbank.

## 3.5.  Stra-tegies

Goals and objectives outlined above shall be achieved by the adoption  and implementation of following  strategies:

- .  Establishing  robust risks assessment  and risk based auditing  process  to focus on bank's  strategy and emerging  high risk areas  such  as strategic, technology  and business  risks in addition  to the banking business specific risks on priority  basis.
 - .  Developing  professionally  standard auditing environment,  culture and practices  through adequate audit related  policies,  procedures, guidelines,  strategy  aligned  departmental  setup, continuous quality review mechanism  etc.
 - .  Having a risk based  audit  software intemally/extemally,  as an audit platform  and database to improve the efficiency ofaudit staff.  Expanding the use oftechnology  and data analytics  tools for engagement planning  execution, reporting and follow  up as well as continuous auditing  approach.
 - .  Initiating  value added audit activities which result in demonstrable and quantifiable  cost savings and/or  evident improvements  in effectiveness  and efficiency ofoperation.
 - .  Enforcing  effective  offsite  review,  monitoring  and follow-up  mechanism  through use of technology  and application  software as required.
 - .  Serving  high quality and objective  audit reports based  on the facts and evidences  to the stakeholden  and continually  improve the alignment  of key stakeholder's expectations  and strategic  business risks with intemal  audit activities.
 - .  Undertaking  additional work at the request  of management,  provided such work does not compromise  the integrity,  objectivity  and independency  principles  of the audit service  or the achievement  ofthe audit plans.
 - .  Assuming a leadership  role in coordinating  the second and third lines ofdefenses  and be a trusted advisor to strategic management  and the Audit Committee  ofthe board.
 - .  Ensuring  effective  co-operation  with top and middle management intemally and with extemal auditors,  other review  bodies  and regulators  to increase  their confidence/trust  on reliability  of intemal  audit function  of the bank.
 - .  Attracting and retaining  approachable,  flexible, courteous  and professional audit staff with strong team ethos,  with the right balance of education,  training, experience,  professional skills and competencies.

## 3.6.  Values

- Integrity: Intemal auditor  shall be straightforward,  honest and truthful.

 <!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- Objectivity: Intemal auditors shall have unbiased  mental attitude that allows  to  perform engagements in such a manner  that they believe  in their work product  and that no quality compromises  are made.
 - Independence: lntemal auditors shall be fiee from any conditions  that threaten  the ability  ofthe intemal  audit activity to carry out intemal  audit responsibilities  in an unbiased  manner.
 - Confidentiality:  Intemal  auditors  shall respect  the confidentiality,  shall  be diligent in the protection of information  acquired  and that they shall not use the information  obtained  in the course of audit for personal  gain  or malicious  action.
 - Due Professional Care, Skills and Competence:  Intemal auditors shall apply the care, skills and competency expected  ofa reasonably  prudent and competent  professional manner.
 - Evidence: The intemal auditor shall,  based on his professional  judgment,  obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to enable  him to draw reasonable  conclusions  on which his/her opinion or findings  can be based.
 - Reporting: The internal auditor  shall carefully  review  and assess the conclusions drawn fiom the audit evidence obtained, as the basis  for his findings  and suggest remedial action.

- The head of intemal  audit department  and other staffs ofthe intemal  audit department  shall have the right to full, free and unrestricted  access to all of the Bank's financial  and operational activities, application  software/systems, records,  property,  personnel and such other sources of information and resources as may be necessary  to carry out their function.  5.1.
 - Applying any techniques of auditing,  as may  be necessfiy  to accomplish the audit activities; 5.2.
 - Obtaining necessary assistance of personnel  in various departments/oflices  of the Bank where the audit is being performed; 5.3.
 - Obtain assistance ofspecialist  from within or outside  the Bank where  considered  necessary; 5.4.
 - Authoriry to seek  explanations,  justifications  from concemed  employees  who have acted in contravention  to the policies, procedures  and guidelines  and who have been acting by compromising  their integrity  and conflict of interest and the issue is known  during the audit process or information  is obtained  through any means.  5.5.
 - Recommend to relevant authority  for disciplinary  or other punishment  actions against employees  who are working against the interest  ofthe bank as per provision ofHR  Bylaws.  5.6.
 - Conduct  surprise visit ofbank's  branches  and departments  including the head office  and seek necessary information that is required to discharge  its duties and responsibilities.  5.7.
 - Any other authority  as delegated to the Intemal  Audit  Department by the Audit  Committee.  5.8.

Internal  audit shall have  the appropriate capability regarding  matters  of regulatory  interest and undertake  regular reviews ofsuch areas based on the results  of its robust risk assessment.  - 6.2.  In particuiar,  the intemal  audit function  shall  review key risk management  functions,  regulatory capital adequacy and liquidity control  functions,  regulatory  and intemal  reporting  functions, the regulatory  compliance  function  and the finance function  ard other areas ofregulatory  interest.
 - 6.3.  Considering the risk profile ofauditable units, availability  ofaudit resources, intemal  audit  shall cover  the areas as stipulated in audit policy ofthe bank.

## 7.3.  Due Professional Care, Skills and Competence

Intemal  auditors shall apply  the care and skills expected of a reasonably  prudent and competent professional.   Due professional  care does not imply infallibility;  however, intemal auditors  having limited competence and experience  in a particular area shall be supervised  by more experienced intemal auditon.  The intemal  auditor shall either  have or obtain such skills and competence,  acquired through general education, technical knowledge  obtained through study  and formal  courses,  as are necessary for the  purpose  of discharging their responsibilities.   The head of intemal audit shall ensure that the intemal  audit  staffacquires  appropriate  ongoing training  in order to meet  the  $owing  technical complexity of banks'  activities and the increasing diversity of tasks that need to be undertaken as a result ofthe  inhoduction  ofnew products and processes  within banls and other developments  in the financial sector.  Intemal auditors  collectively  shall be competent to examine  all areas in which the bank operates.   In exercising  due professional care intemal  auditors  must consider the use of technologr-based  audit and other appropriate data analysis  techniques.

Though the intemal auditor will be entitled  to rely on the work  performed  by other auditors and experts,  they  shall exercise  adequate skill and care in ascertaining their competence  and skills and also in evaluating,  analyzing  and using the results  ofthe work performed  by the experts.

 ## 7.5.  Documentation

The intemal  auditor  shall document matters,  which are important  in providing  evidence  that the audit was carried out in accordance  with the Standards on Intemal Audit and support their findings or the report submitted by them.

The intemal audit department  may frame the audit  programs,  audit procedures  and audit guidelines  for each auditable units  (including  risk based intemal  audit guidelines)  to guide the intemal audit staffs on the process of examining  and evaluating information, documents  etc.  during  audit engagement.

## 12.  Profcssional Standards and Code ofEthics

- lz.t.  All staff members of the department including  head, are required  to ensure  adherence to the highest standards  of professionalism  and ethics, such as those promulgated  by the Institute  of Chartered  Accountants ofNepal.  This shall in no way dilute the obligation  ofevery staffmember to adhere to the bank's employee's  service bylaw or any other regulation as applicable  to all other staff members  ofthe bank by virtue  oftheir  employment  in the bank.
 - 12.2.  Bank  shall have  a separate standards  for intemal  auditors  in compliance  with the Intemational Standards for the Professional Practice in Intemal Auditing oflnstitute oflntemal Auditors  (lIA) and professional standards issued by ICAN.
 - 12.3.  The activities of the head of intemal audit departmen!  as well as those of its staff memben, shall  be carried out in accordance  with the Code ofEthics  for Professional Accountants  in the Business  of the Institute  of Chartered  Accountants of Nepal.

## 13.  Human  Resourcc  Management

- 13.1.  Intemal audit department  staff shall be appointed  with the appropriate  qualifications  and experience, personal qualities  and potential.   The intemal audit department shall be suitably staffed with qualified individuals, who possess  the appropriate experience in order to ensure adequate coverage  ofthe audit environment.
 - 13.2.  Every employee ofthe intemal  audit department  shall have specificjob description  including the knowledge,  skills and abilities required to perform  the duties ofthe position.   It shall also reflect  all the activities and expectations  for that  particular  position.   Job description  ofall the staffs  ofthe intemal  audit department  shall be approved  by head of intemal  audit department.
 - 13.3.  The head ofintemal audit department  has a responsibility  to ensure  that the internal audit team receives  the necessary training  for the performance  of their  duties.  A structured staff development  plan shall be developed  and implemented to ensure that the audit team is provided  with the necessary experience,  training and continuing  professional  education.
 - 13.4.  The head of intemal audit department shall coordinate the training  requirements of intemal audit staff.  This includes the  preparation  and maintenance  oftraining  profiles,  which identif, the training  requirements for different  levels of intemal audit staffs and the maintenance  of personal  training records  for each  individual.
 - 13.5.  Internal audit department  shall have  required  manpower  as determined  by annual internal audit plan.
 - 13.6.  Human  resource required for the department  shall be calculated  based  on the RBIA  Guidelines of the bank.  RBIA guidelines  shall base that more resources  required  for audit of high risk auditable units and less resource required for low risk auditable units.
 - 13.7.  Generally,  fresh and entry  level employees who are not familiar  with banking  activities  and intemal  audit  procedures  are not placed at the department.

## 16.  OutsourcingActivities

- 16.1.  Regardless of whether intemal  audit activities are outsourceq  the audit  committee  remains ultimately  responsible  for the intemal audit  function.   Outsourcing  of intemal audit activities, but not the function, on a limited  and targeted  basis can bring benefits to banks  such as access to specialized exp€rtise  and knowledge  to audit staffs for an intemal audit engagement  where the expertise  is not available  within the intemal  audit function.
 - 16.2.   Additionally,  as a sound  practice, banks shall not outsource intemal audit activities from their own extemal audit firm.
 - 16.3.  The head  of intemal  audit shall ensure  that outsourced  experts/firms  comply with the principles of the bank's intemal audit charter.  The head of intemal audit shall, whenever practical, assimilate  the relevant knowledge input into the intemal  audit function  ofbank  from  outsourced experts/firms.   This shall  be possible  by having one or more  members  ofthe bank's intemal audit staffparticipate  in the extemal expert's work.

## 17.  Relation with Othcr  Functional Arcas

- 17  .1.  The independent  role ofthe  head of intemal  audit department  shall not completely  prohibit the good working relationship  with other departments within the Banl.  Effective relation  and contact  at the appropriate managerial levels before,  during and after the conclusion  of an audit assignment  is essential.
 - The relationship  between a bank's  business units, the support  functions and the intemal audit function  can be explained using the three lines  ofdefense  model.  The business units  are the first line ofdefense.   They underlake  risk within assigned limits of risk exposure  and are responsible and accountable  for identifing,  assessing  and controlling the risks oftheir business.  The second line of defense  includes  the support  functions, such as risk management, compliance,  legal, human resources,  finance,  operations,  and technology.   Each of these functions, in close relationship  with the business units, ensures  that risks in the business/operation units  have been appropriately identified and managed.   The business  support functions  work  closely to help define strategy, implement bank policies and procedures, and collect  information  to create a bank-wide view of risks.  The third line of defense is the intemal audit function  that independently assesses  the effectiveness  ofthe  processes  created  in the first and second lines  of defense and provides assurance  on these  processes.  17.2.
 - The responsibility  for intemal  control  does not transfer liom one line ofdefense  to the next  line whatever be their depth  ofrelationship.  17.3.

## 18.  Relation rvith trxternal  Auditors  and Supcnisors

- 18.1.   The intemal  audit shall liaise, suppor!  coordinate and maintain  a professional relationship  with extemal auditors  and NRB inspection  and supervision  team so as to assist them to carry out their duty smoothly.
 - 18.2.  Intemal auditors shall ensure that enhanced  communication  with Supervisors does not undermine  their respective  perceived  and actual  independence  and status,  as the supervisory authority  and the intemal  audit function  each have different roles  and responsibilities.
 - 18.3.  Supervisors  can have communication  with the bank's intemal  auditors to;
- .  Understand  the risk mitigation measures  taken  by the bank, and
- .  Discuss the risk areas  identified by both  parties,

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

- .  Monitor the bank's response to weaknesses identified.

 18.4.   Similarly,  extemal audit can have harmonious  relation with the intemal auditors by:

- o Periodic meetings  to discuss the audit plans  and activities;
- .  Meeting  between the Intemal  Audit Department  and Edemal  Auditors  to discuss  the annual Intemal and External  Audit  plans;
- o Access  by Extemal  Audit  to the Intemal  Audit  documentation  and vice versa;
- .  Sharing information ofperceived risk areas.
 - o  Exchange of management  letters conceming their respective audit findings  and recommendations.   Intemal Audit may carry out follow-ups on comments and recommendations contained in the Extemal  Audit reports, and vice versa;

Based on the references provided  by Basel  Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS),  Nepal Standards on Auditing  Q. {SAs)  issued  by the Auditing Standard  Board ofNepal,  following modality of communication  shall be enacted  in the bank.

## 21.  Responsibilities of Senior Managcment

In line with the provision  of Audit Policy of Bank regarding  Responsibility of Senior Managemen!  the responsibilities  related  to intemal  audit function  in bank  shall be as follows:

- 21.1.  Senior  management shall be responsible  for developing an internal  control framework that identifies,  measures,  monitors  and controls all risks faced  by the bank.  It shall maintain an organizational  structure  that clearly  assigns  responsibility,  authority  and reporting  relationships and ensues that delegated responsibilities  are effectively  carried  out.  It is an established  practice for senior management  to report to the board ofdirectors  on the scope and performance ofthe intemal  control framework.
 - 21.2.  Senior management  shall inform  the intemal audit function  ofnew  developments,  initiatives, projects,  products  and operational  changes  and ensure  that all associated risks, known  and anticipated, are identified and communicated at an early stage.
 - 21.3.  Senior  management shall be accountable for reviewing  intemal  audit reports,  responding  to intemal audit queries;  ensuring  that timely and appropriate actions  are taken  on all intemal audit fi  ndings  and recommendations.
 - 21.4.  Senior  management shall ensure  that the head  of internal audit has the necessary  resources, financial and otherwise,  available to carry out his or her duties commensurate with the annual intemal  audit plan, scope and budget  approved  by the audit committee.
 - 21.5.  Further, senior  management  is responsible  for:
- .  Ensuring that the intemal audit  department  has the support  ofsenior management;  and direct access  and freedom to report to senior  management;
- .  Proposing the areas ofinvestigation  by intemal  audit;
- o  Inform the head of internal  audit ofany significant intemal control problems, thefu,  fraud, unauthorized transactions  and other lapses.
